instances.label: Grain buyer/merchandiser at a country elevator or processing plant grades incoming truckloads: probe-samples the load, runs moisture, test weight and protein, and inspects the sample for damaged kernels, foreign material, mold, sprouting and live insects to set grade and discounts before the load is dumped.

Buyer or field representative for a processor/packer walks a standing crop (row crop, vegetable, orchard block) before harvest or contracting to judge maturity, stand, expected yield and quality and to look for disease lesions or insect damage.

Produce or tree-nut buyer inspects an arriving lot at a packinghouse, processor receiving dock or distribution center: draws cartons/samples, checks size, color, blemishes, insect damage, decay and internal quality (brix/firmness) to accept, grade and price the lot.

Timber buyer / tree farm contractor cruises a standing timber tract: measures tree diameters, heights and species, judges log grade and defect, and notes insect or disease damage to appraise stumpage value.
Livestock buyer evaluates cattle or hogs at a farm, feedlot or auction barn — condition, muscling, weight, health and defects — to estimate value and bid.

Specialty-product buyer grades leaf or forage at a receiving station or warehouse: tobacco leaf handled bale-by-bale for color, body and quality; hay lots probed and tested for quality; assessing damage, mold and insect evidence.

sources.system: CHS Herman lights-out automated grain elevator (automated truck probe and grading system)
sources.title: CHS automated elevator features 24-hour grain delivery | Feed & Grain
sources.claim: CHS's Herman, MN elevator runs 'lights-out' receiving in which an automatic probe samples each arriving farm truck and the system tests the grain and routes the driver by grade with no employee involved.

sources.system: Cgrain Value automated grain inspection instrument
sources.title: Program Notices - Agricultural Marketing Service - USDA
sources.claim: USDA's Federal Grain Inspection Service has approved Cgrain automated image-analysis equipment for determining an official grade factor (whole kernels) in medium grain ....
sources.transferJustification: Determining an official grade factor on a drawn sample is the same determination a grain buyer makes when grading a delivered lot; USDA approval indicates the machine's output is accepted in place of a licensed grader's factor call.

sources.title: Investigating performance and key factors for real-world deployment of grain image classification using convolutional neural networks (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: The Cgrain Value instrument mechanically singulates and images every kernel of a sample and classifies it into grade-relevant damage classes including Fusarium infection, mold, breakage, spotting and sprouting.
sources.transferJustification: Classifying diseased, moldy, sprouted and broken kernels is precisely the 'locate evidence of disease' and damage-percentage portion of grain grade determination.

sources.title: Grain tool a stickler for quality | Countryman
sources.claim: The EyeFoss grain quality analyzer performs the visual grading checks a human grain grader makes, including insect damage, mould, frost and ... in wheat and barley, at up to 10,000 kernels in four minutes.

sources.system: Spectrim / Spectrim with LUCAi grading platform
sources.title: How citrus packhouses can improve profitability with the latest sorting and grading solutions | TOMRA
sources.claim: TOMRA's Spectrim optical grading platform, installed in citrus and other fruit packhouses worldwide, autonomously grades every fruit for external and internal defects including insect damage, bruising and rot.
sources.transferJustification: Packhouse grading of an incoming fruit lot for defects, insect damage and decay produces the same accept/grade/value determination the produce buyer makes on that lot, on the same objects and to commercial grade tolerances.

sources.title: Solinftec Expands U.S. Footprint 243%, Deploys 100+ Autonomous Robots ... at Commodity Classic 2026
sources.claim: Solinftec reports more than 100 autonomous Solix ... deployed in the US, running sustained field operations across row crops and specialty crops and capturing plant emergence, pest presence and stand gaps.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomously examining a standing crop and reporting pest presence and stand condition is the field form of this task — locating evidence of disease or insect damage and gauging crop condition/value.

sources.title: Solinftec to Release Solix Sprayer Robot for Precise Pesticide Application - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: The Solix robot autonomously scouts commercial fields and reports crop population, weed density and disease identification against thresholds.
sources.transferJustification: Reporting crop population and disease identification in a working field is the examination a buyer performs when inspecting a standing crop for condition and disease/insect damage.

sources.title: Ondas Holdings Says ScottsMiracle-Gro Will Use American Robotics' Autonomous Drones for Crop Analysis - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: American Robotics' Scout drone-in-a-box system flies fully automated crop-analysis missions over commercial fields without a pilot on site, and has been used by ScottsMiracle-Gro for crop analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Repeated automated imaging of a standing crop substitutes for the buyer's walk-through examination of crop condition, stand and visible damage in the field.

sources.title: Treeswift Raises $4.8 Million to Build Next Generation of Forest Monitoring System | Business Wire
sources.claim: Treeswift's SwiftCruise autonomous drones navigate under the forest canopy to extract tree-by-tree measurements, and have been used with commercial timberland owners to estimate timber quantity for value appraisal.
sources.transferJustification: Timber cruising — measuring standing trees to estimate volume and stumpage value — is the tree-farm-contractor form of this task, and SwiftCruise produces the same tree-by-tree measurements the human cruiser collects.

tasks.label: Estimate land production possibilities, surveying property and studying factors such as crop rotation history, soil fertility, or irrigation facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grain buyer/merchandiser visits a Midwest or Plains row-crop farm (corn, soybeans, wheat) before contracting: drives and walks fields with the grower, eyeballs stand and crop condition, reviews the grower's soil test maps and rotation records, looks at tile drainage or a center pivot, and forms an estimate of bushels the acreage can deliver.

Procurement agent for a processor/seed or hay buyer assesses irrigated acreage in the West or Delta: inspects pivots, wells, pumps, ditches and headgates, asks about water allocation, checks soil salinity/fertility reports and prior rotations, and estimates the tonnage the ground can produce under contract.

Buyer for a fruit, nut, or wine-grape packer/processor surveys perennial blocks: walks or drives orchard/vineyard rows, judges crop load, tree/vine vigor, canopy and block uniformity, and produces an estimate of deliverable tonnage and size/quality distribution for procurement planning.

Tree farm contractor / timber buyer cruises a standing tract: traverses the property, measures or samples the stand, judges stem quality and product classes, considers site quality, terrain and access, and estimates merchantable volume and future production potential of the land.

Tobacco buyer or buyer for a diversified small farm walks the grower's fields and facilities: inspects the crop in the field, looks at curing barns, wells or small irrigation setups, discusses rotation and fertility history, and estimates poundage and grade the farm can supply.

sources.title: Autonomous soil sampling: Robo sampling improves accuracy - Top Crop Manager
sources.claim: Rogo Ag's SmartCore soil sampling robot navigates a working farm field on its own to a pre-programmed grid and pulls, bags and seals soil cores, i.e. autonomous in-field soil fertility data collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic soil sampling. It substantiates that a machine can traverse an open farm field and gather soil-fertility inputs, one of the factors named in this task, but not the integrated land-production estimate.

sources.title: Soil Sampling Goes Robotic – DTN (AgFax)
sources.claim: Rogo's robotic soil sampling is sold as a commercial service at large scale on Midwest farm fields, mainly to fertilizer dealers and farmers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soil sampling service in the same open-field environment; shows commercial maturity of field-going robots, but the deliverable is lab samples, not a production estimate.

sources.title: Solinftec Announces First Successful Commercial Season
sources.claim: Solinftec's Solix autonomous solar robots operated commercially through a full season on Indiana and Illinois row-crop farms, scouting fields and monitoring plants while spot-spraying.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crop scouting in row-crop fields. Shows autonomous traversal and plant-level sensing in the same environment, but the output is agronomic alerts, not an estimate of the land's production possibilities.

sources.system: Aerobotics Aeroview citrus yield estimation (drone imagery)
sources.title: Drone Farming: Predicting Yields For Citrus Growers - ADAMA
sources.claim: Aerobotics' drone-based citrus yield estimation product, launched after trials with citrus farms in South Africa and the USA, produced yield estimates more accurate than manual counts.

sources.title: Aerobotics takes one step closer to full roll-out with Yield Estimation trials for Citrus
sources.claim: Aerobotics delivers season-long reports estimating fruit number and size distribution from automated drone flights over orchard blocks, used for packhouse and marketing planning.

sources.title: Green Atlas Cartographer for Precision Crop Load Monitoring | WSU Tree Fruit
sources.claim: Green Atlas Cartographer, a commercial LiDAR/camera sensing platform for orchard crop-load and yield estimation, was validated over the 2024 and 2025 seasons at WSU commercial-scale apple orchard testbeds; the vendor states it can be carried by an autonomous Burro robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: orchard crop-load/yield mapping. Same environment and same output type as the perennial-crop instance, but the platform is usually ATV-mounted, so autonomy is unclear and it is used only as corroboration.

sources.title: Treeswift Raises $4.8 Million to Build Next Generation of Forest Monitoring System
sources.claim: Treeswift's SwiftCruise uses autonomous LiDAR drones flying under the forest canopy to collect tree-level forest inventory data; customers including Weyerhaeuser, Molpus and Superior Pine used it alongside their human timber cruisers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: timber cruising data collection. Same tract environment and overlapping output (volume, product class), but customer statements describe augmenting cruisers rather than delivering the cruise estimate without them.

sources.title: Burro Launches Grande 44, Its Most Powerful Autonomous Work Platform
sources.claim: Burro's autonomous outdoor robots operate at fleet scale in nurseries, vineyards and orchards, logging hundreds of thousands of autonomous miles in rugged outdoor row-crop and perennial settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor navigation in orchard/vineyard rows. Establishes that ground platforms can traverse perennial-crop blocks autonomously, supporting the environment claim for sensor-carrying survey work.

tasks.label: Inspect merchandise or products to determine quality, value, or yield.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vendor/showroom sample appraisal: buyer handles physical samples of new or seasonal merchandise (apparel, home goods, giftware, small electronics) in a corporate office or vendor showroom, feeling materials, checking construction and finish, comparing against the target retail price point and competing items, and forming a quality-versus-value judgment that drives the buy decision.

Market week / trade show / vendor sales call: buyer walks a convention floor or supplier showroom, picking up and examining dozens of unfamiliar products across many booths under crowded, variable conditions, judging quality of construction and materials and estimated value/salability on the spot.

Store floor and backroom walkthrough: buyer inspects displayed and recently received merchandise for condition, wear, defects, and presentation quality, compares competitor product on adjacent shelves, and judges whether quality justifies the price or a markdown/vendor chargeback is warranted.

Receiving inspection at a distribution center or warehouse: buyer or assistant buyer inspects units from an incoming shipment against the purchase spec (correct item, size, color, labeling, visible damage or defects), determines the defect rate of the lot, and accepts, rejects, or claims against the vendor.

Supplier factory or production-run visit: buyer pulls pre-production and production units from the line and checks them against approved specs and workmanship standards (dimensions, color match, stitching/assembly, labeling) to confirm quality before authorizing shipment.

Bulk-lot grading for yield and value: buyer inspects a mixed or raw lot (scrap/recyclable loads, salvage and closeout pallets, rough gemstones, secondhand goods) to grade composition and condition and estimate recoverable yield and resale value before bidding.

sources.title: Amazon Project PI: Generative AI scans your packages for defects - Fast Company
sources.claim: Amazon's Project P.I. runs in imaging tunnels in fulfillment centers, autonomously scanning items moving on conveyors to detect damage, defects, expired dates, and wrong color or size before shipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outbound defect screening of retail merchandise. It is the same act a buyer performs at receiving inspection — judging whether units of consumer merchandise conform in condition, color and size — on the same object class (general retail goods), so performance transfers to conformance-style receiving inspection when items are presented singly on a conveyor.

sources.system: Cognex In-Sight / line scan vision inspection
sources.title: Quality Inspection - Consumer Products | Cognex
sources.claim: Cognex machine vision systems perform pass/fail inspections of consumer products and packaging on production lines and trigger automatic rejection of faulty items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-line assembly and packaging inspection. It covers the same determination a buyer makes on a production sample — does the unit meet the agreed spec for assembly, marking and surface condition — on comparable consumer goods presented in a fixtured station.

sources.system: Elementary vision inspection + Rapid Machine Operator
sources.title: Rapid Robotics and Elementary AI in Automated Inspection | Elementary
sources.claim: Elementary's AI vision inspection paired with a Rapid Robotics machine operator inspects randomly oriented jars one by one for label placement and print legibility, with robotic sorting of failures, in a production plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated label/packaging conformance inspection with robotic handling. Buyers' spec-conformance checks on production units cover the same attributes (correct labeling, print, packaging condition) on similar consumer goods presented to the machine.

sources.title: Shelton Vision Pushes The Needle On AI-Assisted Quality Control | Textile World
sources.claim: Shelton Vision's WebSpector automatically inspects fabric webs at speed, detecting over 98% of faults and applying real-time defect classification and grading rules, i.e., grading material quality automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated textile defect detection and grading. Grading a fabric roll is the same determination a buyer makes on delivered piece goods (defect count and severity, hence usable yield), on the same material, with the web presented to the machine.

sources.title: How Sarine 'Sees' Inside Diamonds, and What it Means for Rough Planning
sources.claim: Sarine's Galaxy systems scan rough ... in an automated scanner and map internal inclusions, producing the data used to assess potential yield and value of the stone; tens of millions of stones have been scanned commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rough-stone yield planning. This is literally the buyer's 'determine value or yield' judgment on a raw lot, performed by a machine into which the stones are loaded.

sources.title: AMP's Horowitz on Bringing AI to the Recycling World | Waste360
sources.claim: AMP Cortex robotic sorters, guided by AMP Neuron vision, identify and physically pick materials from fast-moving conveyors at up to 99% accuracy and ..., deployed in material recovery facilities in North America, Japan and Europe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated characterization and separation of a mixed material stream. Grading a scrap or salvage lot for composition and recoverable yield is the same determination, on the same heterogeneous secondhand material, once the lot is fed onto a sortation line.

sources.title: Simbe Robotics marks 10 years of store intelligence with Tally - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robots autonomously scan store shelves in supermarkets and wholesale clubs, reporting on-shelf availability, price and promotion accuracy and pallet stock; the reported outputs are inventory and price audits, not appraisals of merchandise quality or value.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous retail shelf auditing. Cited to show what store-floor robots actually deliver (stock and price data); it does not substantiate a quality or value determination on merchandise, so it supports no positive judgment here.

instances.label: Residential wind/hail storm claim with exterior-only scope: adjuster drives to a policyholder's home, ladders or otherwise accesses the roof, inspects each facet for hail bruising and creased/torn shingles, checks elevations, gutters, screens and AC fins, photographs and measures the roof, then writes an Xactimate repair estimate. Includes catastrophe-deployment exterior and total-loss inspections after hurricanes/hail swaths.

Residential loss requiring interior scope: pipe break, appliance leak, roof leak, fire/smoke or vandalism. Adjuster walks furnished, cluttered rooms, moves and inspects contents, opens closets, checks attics and crawlspaces, takes moisture readings, room-by-room measurements, evaluates cause of loss and writes an interior repair and contents scope.

Commercial or multi-family exterior/roof-only loss: hail or wind damage on a big-box store, warehouse, church or apartment-complex roof; adjuster inspects membrane/shingle facets, HVAC units and flashings, takes test squares and measurements, and prepares or reviews a roof replacement estimate on premises controlled by the building owner or property manager.

Commercial or large-loss property claim with interior and complex causation: fire, flood or structural loss at a business, apartment building or industrial facility; adjuster inspects interiors, equipment and stock, coordinates with engineers and restoration contractors, and creates or reviews a multi-trade estimate including code upgrades.

Auto/vehicle physical damage claim handled by the adjuster: inspect a damaged vehicle at a collision shop, drive-in claim center or tow/salvage yard, verify reported damage against the loss facts, and write or review the repair estimate / total-loss valuation.

Desk or virtual handling with no site visit: examiner reviews a contractor's, public adjuster's or field vendor's property damage estimate line by line against photos, measurements and price lists, negotiates or corrects the scope, or creates the estimate directly from photos/video the insured or a vendor submitted.

It does not transfer to interior loss adjusting: Spot captures imagery/scans along pre-taught routes but does not move contents, access attics/crawlspaces, take moisture readings, determine cause of loss, or produce an interior repair scope.

instances.label: Routine license check at a restaurant, bar, or retail storefront: officer arrives unannounced during business hours at a site never visited by that inspector before, identifies self to the manager, walks the premises to locate posted business/food-service/occupancy licenses (framed on a wall, behind a counter, in a back office), reads them, checks name, address, expiry and conditions against agency records, photographs them, and documents whether licensing standards (signage, posted permits, permitted activity) are upheld; issues a notice or citation on the spot if deficient.

Personal-service establishment (hair/nail salon, barbershop, tattoo or massage business): verify the establishment license is displayed and, additionally, that each individual practitioner working that day has a current, displayed personal license matching the person present; inspect sanitation/sterilization practices required as a licensing condition; question workers who may be evasive or non-English speaking.

Licensed care facility visit (child care center, adult day program, group home): verify the license and capacity/age-range certificate are posted, walk the building to check licensing standards (exits, medication storage, staff-child ratios), cross-check staff credential and background-check files against the people present, and hold an exit conference with the director.

Alcohol, tobacco, or cannabis retail compliance visit with an enforcement component: verify the state license and required warning signage are posted and current, observe sales practices and age-verification at the register (sometimes with an underage decoy), inspect the licensed area boundaries and hours conditions, take statements, and serve a violation notice.

Construction or trade job site: verify the building permit placard is posted and matches the work in progress, verify the contractor's and subcontractors' licenses and any specialty certifications, check that unlicensed work is not occurring; outdoor, cluttered, changing site with heavy equipment and workers who may not be cooperative.

Mobile or temporary operation: food truck, sidewalk/farmers-market vendor, temporary event stand, or for-hire vehicle inspected at the curb, a fairground, or a depot; verify the permit decal/placard is displayed and valid for that location and date, check the operator's individual permit, and verify basic operating standards outdoors in traffic and weather.

sources.title: Automated Inspections Made Simple | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, reading gauges and capturing visual/thermal data, but each mission must first be recorded by a human manually driving the robot along the exact route and specifying the actions at each point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine walking inspection rounds in a facility, reading posted analog instruments and equipment states. It is the closest deployed analogue to an inspector's walk-through, but the mission must be taught per site, so it cannot handle a first-time visit to an arbitrary establishment, and it does not verify documents against a licensing database, question staff, or issue findings.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot is commercially deployed for autonomous data-collection missions across industrial customer sites; manipulation such as opening doors and picking up objects is largely operator-driven rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated inspection walk-throughs of factories, power plants and construction sites. Establishes the environments (owner-controlled industrial facilities on pre-mapped routes) where autonomous inspection robots actually work, which is narrower than the varied third-party establishments a compliance officer visits.

sources.title: How Simbe Robotics' retail robots help stores and brands
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously navigates occupied retail stores and reads posted printed information (barcodes, price and promotion tags), flagging discrepancies; it is commercially deployed across many chains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously reading posted printed documents in a working retail business and reporting discrepancies, which resembles reading a posted license. Transfer is limited: Tally runs pre-mapped routes down open aisles in stores that host it, does not search unfamiliar premises or behind counters, does not verify credentials against a regulator's records, and makes no judgment about whether operating standards are upheld.

sources.title: Parking | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol parking areas and campuses on defined outdoor routes, using automatic license plate recognition to flag unauthorized or blacklisted vehicles and alerting human operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously checking whether vehicles present are authorized, i.e., a permit/authorization check by machine vision. Transfer is limited: it matches plates against a list on a fixed patrol route on premises its client controls, and it escalates to human officers rather than verifying licensing standards or closing out an inspection.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine detection of licensing/regulatory violations in a public setting. It remains a three-week trial that only flags suspected behaviours to human officers; it does not enter establishments, verify licence documents, or complete an inspection.

tasks.label: Investigate complaints and suspected violations regarding illegal dumping, pollution, pesticides, product quality, or labeling laws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Illegal/open dumping complaint: inspector drives to a roadside pull-off, vacant lot, ravine or rural parcel reported by a citizen; locates and photographs the debris pile, records GPS and volume, sifts through bags/drums/tires for identifying evidence (mail, invoices, license plates), screens for hazardous or asbestos-containing material, interviews the complainant, neighbors and landowner, and issues a notice of violation or cleanup order with a written case file.

Pollution complaint at a permitted industrial or commercial facility (odor, visible smoke, discharge, improper waste storage): unannounced entry, opening conference with plant staff, walk-through of process areas, tank farms and outfalls, visible-emissions reading, collection of a wastewater/waste sample with chain of custody, review of manifests, logs and permit conditions, staff interviews, and a compliance determination and inspection report.

Pesticide complaint (drift onto neighboring crops/homes, misapplication, damaged vegetation or bee kill, worker exposure): visit to farm field, orchard or residential property; interviews with complainant and applicator; collection of foliage, soil or surface swipe samples; inspection of application equipment, product containers and labels; review of application records and weather data; comparison against label directions and a violation determination.

Water/stormwater/spill or sewage complaint outdoors: inspector walks a creek bank, ditch, wetland, construction site or failing septic area in variable weather and terrain, traces a discharge upstream to its source, takes field measurements (pH, DO, turbidity, conductivity), collects grab samples, photographs erosion or sheen, identifies the responsible party, and documents findings.

Product quality/labeling complaint at a retailer, distributor or warehouse (e.g., unregistered or misbranded pesticide, mislabeled fuel or consumer product): locate the product in stock, examine the label against registration and labeling law, photograph, collect an official sample for lab analysis, issue a stop-sale/hold order, interview management and trace the distribution chain, and file the report.

sources.system: ANYmal with Gas Leak and Presence Detection
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: ANYmal legged robots run autonomous inspection missions inside operating industrial facilities (energy, metals, mining, oil and gas) and can locate gas leak sources, quantify loss and alert staff — a sensing sub-step of a facility pollution inspection, without sampling, records review, interviews or a compliance determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine autonomous plant inspection. It shares the walk-the-facility sensing element of an odor/leak complaint investigation at an industrial site, but covers only detection on pre-taught routes, not evidence sampling, records review, interviews, or a violation determination.

sources.title: Percepto Drone Regulation | BVLOS & Industrial Safety
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box performs automated beyond-visual-line-of-sight inspection flights over industrial sites and substations with no on-site personnel, producing imagery and AI-derived findings; it does not collect physical samples or make regulatory determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated aerial site monitoring at fixed industrial premises. It substantiates autonomous visual data capture at a controlled facility, comparable to the observational portion of a pollution complaint visit, but not the sampling, interviewing or case-file portions.

sources.title: Dominion Energy | Boston Dynamics case study
sources.claim: Spot conducted autonomous radiation surveys at an operating utility nuclear site in a pilot, matching a technician's survey coverage with more consistent data — evidence of autonomous mobile field measurement inside a controlled facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: radiological survey rounds. Shows a legged robot can autonomously take field readings along set routes in a structured facility; it does not show ad hoc investigation of a complaint, sample chain of custody, or interviewing.

sources.title: Harvesting plant data with robotics, sensors and advanced computing | ORNL
sources.claim: A research ground robot demonstrated independent collection of soil samples for environmental data collection — a single sub-step of a field pollution or pesticide investigation, at research-demonstration maturity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soil sampling for research. Comparable object handling to collecting a soil sample in a pesticide or dumping investigation, but a laboratory/field research demo covering only sample acquisition, not legally defensible evidence handling or investigative judgment.

sources.title: Oakland Plots AI Drone Patrols To Bust Illegal Dumpers
sources.claim: Municipal use of drones against illegal dumping is at the surveillance/pilot-proposal stage: aerial systems would detect and report dumping at hotspots, with human investigators identifying responsible parties and pursuing enforcement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial detection of dumping. Even if flown, it only spots dumping events; the complaint investigation — site examination, evidence recovery, interviews, violation determination — remains human work, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

instances.label: Routine RCRA generator inspection at a mid-size or large manufacturing plant: inspector walks the production floor and the 90-day accumulation area escorted by plant EHS staff, checks each drum/tote for a legible hazardous-waste label and accumulation start date, closed lids, bungs, corrosion or leakage, incompatible neighbors, aisle space, secondary containment and spill kits, photographs findings, cross-checks container inventory against logs and manifests, and issues a compliance determination/report.

Small-quantity generator inspection at a small business (auto body/repair shop, dry cleaner, metal plater, printer, university or clinic lab): cluttered back rooms, mixed drums, pails, cabinets and shelves of solvents and acids in layouts that differ site to site, unmarked or homemade containers, satellite accumulation points near workbenches, outdoor waste-oil tanks; inspector identifies containers, judges labeling/closure/segregation and asks staff how wastes are handled.

Periodic inspection of a permitted TSDF or dedicated hazardous-waste/chemical storage building: rows of palletized drums in a warehouse or tank farm, recurring (weekly/monthly) container-condition and storage-compliance rounds, container integrity and marking checks before wastes move to disposal, containment and tank inspections, logged in an inspection record.

Complaint, spill or illegal-disposal investigation at an uncontrolled site: roadside or vacant-lot drum dumping, abandoned property, farm or contractor yard, a release into a ditch; inspector locates and identifies unknown containers/substances, screens hazards, takes photographs and samples with chain of custody, traces the generator, and documents violations.

Disposal-chain verification at a shipping dock: inspector observes loading of hazardous-waste containers onto a transporter, verifies DOT markings, labels, placards and container condition on the outgoing shipment, checks that containers match the manifest line items and that the receiving TSDF is permitted, and signs off/records the verification.

sources.system: Robotic ultrasonic drum testing system (Advanced Mixed Waste Treatment Project)

sources.title: Robotic Technology Gives Idaho a Hand in Waste Drum Scans to Positive Reviews
sources.claim: A robotic ultrasonic-testing arm inside a waste storage building at the Idaho National Laboratory Site scans each legacy transuranic hazardous-waste drum and determines whether it meets the DOT minimum wall-thickness requirement, gating compliant shipment for disposal; more than 2,000 drums screened since March 2025 under RCRA work scope.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying that hazardous-waste containers meet a regulatory (DOT/RCRA) storage-and-shipment standard. Same objects (55/100-gallon hazardous-waste drums), same output (pass/fail regulatory determination that gates disposal), performed at a purpose-built station where drums are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Efficient vision inspection system for label accuracy - Bizerba LabelSecure
sources.claim: Commercial inline machine-vision label verification systems check presence and content of labels on containers moving through a packaging line and automatically reject non-conforming units, producing auditable quality records.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated verification that a container carries the correct, legible regulatory labeling. The labeling element of hazardous-chemical container compliance (correct hazard/contents text, legibility) is the same perception-and-decision problem on containers presented at a fixtured station.

sources.system: Label print inspection AI camera (Qualitas machine-vision OCR)
sources.title: OCR in Manufacturing: How Machine Vision Reads Labels, Codes & Characters Automatically
sources.claim: Machine-vision OCR systems in production read lot codes, manufacturing and expiry dates and identifiers on each unit, verify them against master data and record a pass/fail flag, catching partial or ghosted date printing that human end-of-line checkers miss.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated reading and rule-checking of dates on container labels. Verifying an accumulation start date is within the 90/180-day limit is the same OCR-plus-rule check on a container presented to the machine.

sources.title: ANYmal X Tested for Autonomous Robot Inspections in Ex-zones at BASF
sources.claim: An explosion-proof legged robot performs autonomous inspection rounds inside operating chemical plant Ex-zones, collecting equipment condition and anomaly data at BASF's Ludwigshafen steamcracker and Oxo plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous walk-through inspection rounds in a chemical facility. Shows what mobile robots achieve in an E2 chemical plant today (gauge/thermal/anomaly data on fixed assets), not container-level hazardous-waste compliance determinations.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR and FLIR MUVE C360
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A quadruped robot running autonomous inspection rounds at a 40-acre midstream gas plant detected a combustible gas plume from a pinhole leak using gas, visual and thermal payloads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection of a release inside a process facility. It substantiates mobile leak sensing in an E2 facility but not the labeling, dating, closure, containment and records checks that make up a hazardous-chemical compliance inspection.

sources.system: ARIES (Autonomous Robotic Inspection Experimental System); related SWAMI
sources.developer: SCUREF/Clemson for USDOE; Savannah River Technology Center (SWAMI)
sources.title: Low-level stored waste inspection using mobile robots (Conference) | OSTI.GOV
sources.claim: A mobile robot was developed for DOE to carry out the routine, regulated inspection of drums of hazardous/radioactive waste stored in warehouse aisles, navigating three-foot aisles, judging drum surface condition and maintaining a per-drum database; a prototype only, from the 1990s, and DOE drum stores are still inspected by people.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the storage-inspection variant of this task (regulated periodic inspection of stored hazardous-waste containers), but at 1990s prototype maturity with no evidence of worker-quality operational use, so it does not establish E2 completion today.

sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control | TechTarget
sources.claim: Autonomous inventory drones fly warehouse aisles and read barcodes, lot codes and expiration dates on stored pallets, reporting exceptions to the warehouse system far faster than manual scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous label and date reading of stored goods in a structured facility. It covers only the label/date-capture element; no cited system judges closure, corrosion, containment, segregation or issues a compliance determination in an E2 storage building.

instances.label: NPDES / drinking-water or wastewater treatment plant compliance inspection: inspector walks the plant with the operator, records influent/effluent flow-meter and totalizer readings, chlorine-residual and other on-line analyzer values, checks chemical feed tank levels, observes unit processes, solids handling and the outfall, takes field measurements (pH, DO, temperature) and an effluent grab sample, then logs and reports the data. Institution-controlled facility, fixed layout, steel walkways and stairs, wet and noisy.

Industrial facility inspection (air, RCRA hazardous waste, or industrial stormwater) at a refinery, chemical plant, foundry, food plant or power station: walk process and storage areas, record CEMS/parameter monitor readouts, pressure and flow gauges, tank and scrubber levels, observe leaks, visible emissions, stained ground, container labeling and secondary containment; photograph and write up findings. Controlled industrial premises, indoor and outdoor.

Small commercial premises inspection (gas station underground storage tanks, dry cleaner, auto shop, small-quantity hazardous waste generator): read the tank monitoring console and gauges, check spill buckets, containment, vapor recovery, waste container conditions, record readings and conditions on a checklist form. Operator-controlled retail/commercial site with a standard layout, customers and vehicles present.

Construction-site stormwater (CGP/SWPPP) inspection, often within 24-48 h of a rain event: walk the active site and its perimeter over mud, spoil piles and slopes, check silt fence, inlet protection, stabilized entrances, concrete washout and stabilization, observe discharge points and sediment-laden runoff, photograph, log rainfall and findings.

Ambient/field water work at a stream, ditch, lagoon, or pipe outfall away from any facility: locate the discharge point, measure or estimate flow, take field probe readings (pH, DO, conductivity, temperature, chlorine), collect grab samples into bottles with chain-of-custody, note odor, color, foam and bank conditions; access by wading, bank or bridge.

Rural or open-site inspection / complaint response: CAFO or farm waste lagoon, open burning, illegal dumping, spill or fuel-release site. Inspector drives to a site of unknown layout, walks uneven ground, observes and photographs conditions, takes handheld instrument readings (e.g., PID, lagoon freeboard, odor observations), and records findings for the file.

instances.label: Compliance sampling at a permitted POTW or industrial outfall: inspector selects the effluent sample point, sets up/programs a flow-paced 24-hour composite autosampler (or retrieves one), keeps the composite iced/refrigerated to <=6 C, transfers to labeled containers, completes chain of custody. On an operating plant site.

Grab sampling at a facility for parameters that must be grab-collected (pH, oil & grease, VOCs, bacteria, residual chlorine, cyanide/sulfide): inspector walks the site, opens a manhole or sample tap, dips or fills pre-preserved bottles and headspace-free VOA vials, adds acid/base preservative, reads field parameters, ices and documents.

Ambient/receiving-water sampling from a boat, bridge, dock or shoreline of a lake, river, harbor, or reservoir (upstream/downstream of a discharge, complaint or spill/fish-kill response): lower bottles or a Kemmerer/Van Dorn to depth at chosen stations, take field readings, transfer to preserved containers on ice.

Wading or bank sampling of a small creek, drainage ditch, seep, or agricultural runoff channel immediately up- and downstream of a suspected discharge: pick the mixing-zone point, step through mud/vegetation/riprap, dip-fill bottles avoiding sediment, preserve and ice on the tailgate.

Stormwater/MS4 outfall sampling during a rain event: locate the outfall pipe, ditch, or catch basin, capture a first-flush grab within the first 30 minutes of discharge and/or deploy a rain/flow-triggered automatic sampler, then preserve and ice the aliquots.

Groundwater compliance sampling at a landfill or remediation site: purge a monitoring well with a dedicated low-flow pump until field parameters stabilize, fill preserved bottles and VOA vials from the discharge line, ice and document.

instances.label: Pretreatment compliance inspection of a permitted industrial user (metal finisher, food processor, plating shop, industrial laundry) discharging to a POTW: walk the pH/neutralization, clarifier and oil-water separator units, verify the permitted sampling point and flow meter, look for unpermitted bypasses and spill containment, collect an effluent grab sample at the sampling manhole, review self-monitoring records and interview the operator.

NPDES compliance evaluation inspection of a municipal wastewater treatment plant: traverse headworks, aeration basins, clarifiers, disinfection and sludge handling on outdoor catwalks and stairs, check flow measurement and calibration, inspect the lab and QA records, observe the outfall and collect a sample, and evaluate operations against permit limits.

Inspection of a solid waste landfill or transfer station: drive/walk the active working face and haul roads, check daily cover, litter and waste screening, leachate collection levels and gas wellhead readings, surface emission and stormwater controls, and review operating records; terrain and waste change daily and heavy equipment is working.

RCRA hazardous waste generator or TSDF inspection: examine container storage and satellite accumulation areas for labeling, accumulation dates, closed lids, aisle space and secondary containment integrity, inspect tanks and their overfill controls, and reconcile inventory against manifests and logs, indoors and in outdoor pads at an industrial plant.

Complaint-driven or small-source inspection at an unstructured site: failing onsite septic or small package treatment system at a private property, illegal dumping or unpermitted waste disposal on a rural parcel or roadside; the inspector locates the discharge, documents conditions photographically, may take a sample, and cites conditions taken as found.

tasks.label: Inspect government property, such as construction sites or public housing, to ensure compliance with contract specifications or legal requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine progress/conformance walk of an active publicly funded construction site (building or infrastructure): traverse the site on a repeatable route, photograph and scan installed work, compare as-built conditions against contract drawings/BIM, log quantities and deviations for the periodic inspection report.

Hands-on construction verification on the same kind of site: measure rebar spacing/cover and slopes before a pour, check material tags and delivery tickets, probe backfill, open covers, verify hold points and safety compliance, and discuss corrections face-to-face with the contractor's superintendent.

Occupied public-housing dwelling unit inspection (NSPIRE/UPCS-style): enter the tenant's apartment, press-test smoke/CO alarms, trip GFCI outlets, run faucets and check under sinks for leaks, open windows and doors, check appliances, look for mold/pests among the tenant's belongings, and record deficiencies.

Condition inspection of common and support areas of a housing development or government building controlled by the agency: corridors, stairwells, laundry and mechanical rooms, roofs, parking and grounds — checking lighting, exit signage, fire extinguishers, leaks, trip hazards and equipment condition.

Service-contract compliance walkthrough at a government facility (federal building, courthouse, base): verify the custodial/grounds/maintenance contractor performed the statement of work — restroom and floor cleanliness, trash removal, lamp replacement, landscaping — and document deficiencies for payment deduction.

Government property and equipment audit at an agency warehouse, motor pool, or contractor plant: locate tagged government-furnished property, verify existence, location, quantity and visible condition against the property records, and report discrepancies.

tasks.label: Collect, identify, evaluate, or preserve case evidence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field documentation of conditions as case evidence: inspector drives to a contractor jobsite, government property parcel, roadway project or damaged equipment yard, photographs/videos the deficient conditions from multiple angles with scale, timestamp and GPS reference, and preserves the imagery in the case file.

Facility walkthrough evidence capture: inspector tours a contractor's plant, depot or warehouse holding government property, records the condition, markings and serial/tag numbers of equipment and stored items with photos and notes, and preserves the record as case documentation.

Documentary/records evidence: at the inspected entity's office, the inspector locates contract files, invoices, receiving reports and logs, copies or scans them (or takes originals), marks each item with case number and date, bags/folders and inventories them, and signs a chain-of-custody form.

Physical sample or item collection: inspector takes a specimen or item (material or fuel sample, defective component, mislabeled product, seized government-owned item) at a facility or field site, places it in a container/evidence bag, seals it tamper-evident, labels it with case ID and source, and transports it to a lab or evidence room.

Evidence intake and preservation at the agency office: repackaging, labeling and bar-coding received items, logging them into the evidence management system, placing them in the secured evidence room/locker in the correct location, and retrieving them later for review or hand-off.

Examining collected physical evidence: comparing a delivered part or material sample against contract specifications (dimensions, markings, serial numbers, grade), measuring or testing it, and recording the findings as part of the case file.

tasks.label: Submit samples of products to government laboratories for testing, as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a contractor's plant or warehouse, the inspector draws a sample of discrete manufactured product from a lot (fasteners, textiles, packaged rations, electronic parts): selects the required units per the sampling plan, seals them in a bag or box, attaches the sample identification tag and chain-of-custody paperwork, and packs the carton for shipment to the designated government test lab. Indoor industrial facility, fixed layout, controlled access, forklifts and staff moving about.

On an active highway or construction project (or the supplying materials plant), the inspector obtains a field sample of bulk construction material - aggregate or soil from a stockpile, hot-mix asphalt from a haul truck, fresh concrete from a truck chute - scoops it into pails, splits it to test size, seals and labels the containers, and readies them for the state materials laboratory. Outdoors, uneven ground, traffic, weather, equipment moving.

At a fuel depot, bulk terminal or chemical storage facility, the inspector draws a sample of a liquid product (jet fuel, diesel, lubricant, coating) from a tank sample point, drum or loading line into approved bottles, caps and seals them, labels, completes hazmat/DOT shipping paperwork, and packs the bottles in an approved shipping container for the government lab. Controlled industrial premises with hazardous-area rules.

Back at the government field office, the inspector logs accumulated samples into the lab information system, packs them into shipping cartons with padding, absorbent or cold packs, prints and applies the lab submission forms and shipping labels, and hands the parcels to the courier or mailroom for dispatch. Ordinary office setting with desks, supply cabinets, printers.

The inspector hand-carries the packaged samples by vehicle to the government laboratory (state materials lab, USDA/AMS lab, DLA lab), drives public roads, parks, carries the box to the receiving window, and completes the custody transfer/receipt with lab intake staff.

sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously runs deliveries of lab samples, supplies and medications through hospital corridors and elevators; deployed in more than 25 ... hospital facilities with over 1.25 million autonomous deliveries.

tasks.label: Inspect government-owned equipment or materials in the possession of private contractors to ensure compliance with contracts or regulations or to prevent misuse.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Contractor warehouse/storeroom holding government-furnished material: inspector walks racked aisles, samples records, locates specific line items, reads property/IUID barcode or RFID tags, counts quantities, checks that items are marked, segregated from contractor-owned stock, and stored in serviceable condition; reconciles findings against the contractor's property records.

Contractor production floor or shop: inspector locates government-furnished tooling, special test equipment, jigs and machine tools in active use, verifies identification plates and tags, checks physical condition, calibration/maintenance status, and that the equipment is being used on the authorized contract rather than diverted to commercial work; moves among operating machinery and workers.

Outdoor contractor-controlled yards, motor pools and laydown areas, plus active construction/field sites under government contract: inspector inspects government-furnished vehicles, generators, trailers, containers and material stockpiles in the open — presence, hour meters, damage, weather exposure, evidence of unauthorized or personal use — under varying weather and shifting site layout.

Contractor office and laboratory spaces: inspector spot-checks accountable IT and communications property (laptops, test sets, radios, instruments) at desks, in cabinets, lockers and lab benches, matching serial numbers/barcodes to the accountability record and noting missing, unmarked or misused items.

Sensitive and high-value government property in secure storage at a contractor site: arms, ammunition, controlled cryptographic or classified hardware in locked cages, safes and sealed containers; requires 100% serial-number count, seal integrity checks, opening/closing containers and escorted access.

Depot, hangar or shipyard where large government assets (aircraft, vehicles, engines, vessels) are held under a maintenance or overhaul contract: inspector examines the asset's exterior and condition, verifies configuration and identification, documents damage, and checks handling/storage practices against contract terms.

sources.title: Verity inventory drones surpass 100 warehouse sites, including UPS - Automated Warehouse

The physical act is the same as verifying government property in a contractor storeroom — traverse racked aisles, read item identification labels at each location, and reconcile physical presence against a record system, flagging discrepancies.

sources.claim: Gather AI drones fly autonomous missions through customer warehouses photographing pallet locations; the platform's core use cases include location validation and damage detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse inventory audit with damage detection. Comparable objects (palletized stock and labels), comparable precision (label-level identification), and the same structured-facility environment as a contractor storeroom holding government material.

sources.title: Near Earth Autonomy Develops Aircraft Inspection By Drone
sources.claim: Boeing and Near Earth Autonomy demonstrated autonomous drone inspection of an Air Force C-5M Super Galaxy at Dover AFB, with the drone navigating the aircraft and imaging its exterior for defect review.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior condition inspection of a government-owned aircraft in a military maintenance setting — the same asset type and inspection output a property inspector documents at a contractor depot.

sources.system: ATT Automated Inspection System / FANUC iRVision robotic inspection cells
sources.title: Collaborative Robot Quality Inspection | CRX Collaborative Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: Pre-configured robotic inspection cells with robot-mounted 3D scanners and vision perform repeatable dimensional and visual inspection of parts presented to them on the factory floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated part inspection in a fixtured cell. At E1 the property item is presented to the machine; verifying its identification markings, completeness and physical condition is the same sensing-and-judgment act performed by these cells.

sources.title: How Deep Learning Automates Verification, Classification and Defect Detection in Packaging
sources.claim: Deep-learning industrial OCR/OCV systems read and verify serial, date and lot markings on parts and plates automatically on production lines, including deformed or poorly etched metal marks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated marking verification on a production line. Supplies the identification step (reading serial/IUID plates and confirming they match the record) for a fixtured E1 inspection station handling government property.
