roles.title: Coroners
roles.description: Direct activities such as autopsies, pathological and toxicological analyses, and inquests relating to the investigation of deaths occurring within a legal jurisdiction to determine cause of death or to fix responsibility for accidental, violent, or unexplained deaths.

tasks.label: Complete death certificates, including the assignment of cause and manner of death.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform medicolegal examinations and autopsies, conducting preliminary examinations of the body to identify victims, locate signs of trauma, and identify factors that would indicate time of death.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scene response to an unattended death in a private residence or outdoors (bedroom floor, bathroom, vehicle, wooded area). The coroner examines the body where found: flexes joints for rigor, presses skin to test lividity blanching, takes body and ambient temperature, moves/rolls the body to inspect the back and posterior scalp for wounds, checks for injection sites and injuries, confirms identity from ID, tattoos or family, photographs the body in situ, and documents findings before release to transport.

Preliminary examination of a death occurring inside an institution (hospital room, nursing home bed, jail cell, dialysis unit). Body is on a bed or floor in a controlled facility; the coroner externally examines for trauma, decubiti, therapeutic artifacts (lines, tubes, resuscitation marks), notes postmortem changes for time-of-death estimation, and verifies identity from wristband and staff.

Morgue external examination: body received in a bag at the medical examiner/coroner facility, weighed and measured, clothing removed and retained as evidence, trace evidence collected, body washed and turned, all wounds and marks described, measured and photographed, fingerprints or footprints taken for identification, postmortem interval indicators (rigor, livor, decomposition, vitreous sampling) recorded.

Full medicolegal autopsy in an autopsy suite: Y-incision, chest plate removal, evisceration, organ-by-organ dissection and weighing, skull opening with saw and brain removal, dissection of neck and wound tracks, collection of toxicology and histology specimens, then reconstruction and closure of the body.

Examination of decomposed, burned, fragmented or skeletonized remains at the morgue/anthropology bench for identification (dental charting, radiographic comparison, anthropological profile), detection of skeletal or thermal trauma, and estimation of postmortem interval from decomposition state and entomology.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich / University of Bern (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0, a rail-mounted six-axis industrial robot in a purpose-built forensic imaging suite at an institute of forensic medicine, performs automated 3D surface documentation of corpses and CT-guided needle placement for post-mortem tissue and liquid sampling — documentation and sampling sub-steps only, not an external examination or autopsy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic post-mortem imaging/documentation and needle biopsy on the same objects (human corpses) in the same institutions. It covers only surface capture and needle sampling; it does not undress, turn, palpate or dissect the body, so it does not transfer to completing the medicolegal examination.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtual Autopsy Connects Radiology and Forensics (RSNA News)
sources.claim: The Virtobot robotic system is in routine use alongside a CT scanner at a forensic medicine institute, providing automated high-resolution 3D surface documentation and CT-guided post-mortem tissue sampling as an adjunct to human forensic examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated forensic imaging/documentation of bodies in a medicolegal institute. Shows deployment of the only robot routinely used on decedents, but its output is imaging data interpreted by pathologists, not a completed preliminary examination or autopsy.

sources.system: Mobile autonomous surface scanning robot for legal medicine
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology / University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf (Institute of Legal Medicine)
sources.title: A Mobile Robotic Approach to Autonomous Surface Scanning in Legal Medicine (arXiv 2502.14514; IJCARS 2026)
sources.claim: A mobile robot with a 6-joint arm and RGB-D camera autonomously plans and performs full-body surface scans of actual corpses in a legal medicine facility (~92% surface coverage); it captures external documentation only and complements, rather than replaces, the manual external examination and post-mortem CT.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous external documentation of corpses in a morgue — same objects and setting as the coroner's external examination. It only images the exposed surface; it does not undress, roll, palpate, sample, or make findings, so it cannot complete the examination instance.

sources.system: Virtobot (as characterized by the Hamburg group)
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology / UKE Institute of Legal Medicine
sources.title: A Mobile Robotic Approach to Autonomous Surface Scanning in Legal Medicine (arXiv 2502.14514)
sources.claim: The same group notes that the established robotic forensic installation requires a dedicated room, thorough manual preparation of the body and manual marker placement plus manual path planning — i.e., humans still handle and prepare the decedent for the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic corpse documentation. Establishes that body handling and preparation in the morgue remain manual, so no cited system performs the handling steps of a medicolegal external examination.

sources.developer: Department of Forensic Medicine, Chulalongkorn University
sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Surgery for Cadaveric Skull Opening: A New Method of Autopsy Procedure (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: A robotic autopsy saw was evaluated for cadaveric skull opening at a forensic medicine department, addressing noise and aerosol exposure during one cutting step of the autopsy; the study reports a robotic-assisted method rather than an autonomous system performing the autopsy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted cutting during autopsy. Even this narrowest dissection sub-step is assisted rather than autonomous, and no evisceration, organ dissection or documentation is performed, so it cannot substantiate completing an autopsy.

sources.title: 'Spot' the robot dog assists Mass. State Police in high-risk situations
sources.claim: Robots fielded by US police at death and crime scenes are teleoperated quadrupeds used for standoff reconnaissance and scene documentation; they do not handle or examine bodies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic presence at death/crime scenes. It is operator-driven and performs no contact examination of a decedent, so no capability transfers to scene-side medicolegal examination.

tasks.label: Interview persons present at death scenes to obtain information useful in determining the manner of death.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Observe and record the positions and conditions of bodies and related evidence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unattended/unexpected death in a private residence (natural death or suspected overdose): the coroner or death investigator enters a cluttered home found as-is, records the body's position relative to furniture and objects, examines the decedent (lividity pattern, rigor, skin condition, body temperature, injuries under clothing), notes medications, notes, weapons or paraphernalia nearby, takes photographs and measurements, and writes a scene narrative. Family, pets, police and EMS artifacts are often present.

Death inside an institutional facility (hospital room, nursing home, hospice, correctional cell): the investigator responds to a room with fixed layout and staff control, records the body's position in bed or on the floor, documents medical devices/lines, decubitus ulcers, restraints or trauma, photographs the room and body, and records condition findings for the case file.

Documentation of a body received at the coroner's morgue/autopsy suite: body on a tray or table, investigator/technician photographs the body as received, documents clothing and personal effects, identifying features, evidence of medical intervention, wounds and decomposition state, and records these observations in the case record before or during the external examination.

Outdoor or public violent/traumatic death scene (motor vehicle crash on a roadway, shooting in a street or parking lot, industrial fatality): work under weather, traffic and time pressure alongside police crime-scene units; record body position relative to vehicles/weapons/debris, condition and injuries, coordinate documentation and photographs.

Recovery-type scene: decomposed, skeletonized, burned, submerged or fragmented remains in a field, wooded area, water body or fire debris; record position and scatter of remains and associated evidence, condition of tissue, insect activity, in terrain taken as found.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (with University Hospital Zurich)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0 is a robot system installed at the Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich that performs automated whole-body surface and wound documentation (photogrammetry plus optical 3D scanning) of corpses presented on the scanner table in a dedicated robot-equipped forensic imaging suite, and is used routinely for surface documentation in casework.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: the machine produces the photographic/3D record of a decedent's external condition (wounds, surface) for the medicolegal file, which is the 'record the condition of bodies' output, though it requires the body to be placed, undressed and turned by staff and the ceiling/floor-mounted arm needs a dedicated room.

sources.system: Mobile robotic full-body RGB-D surface scanning system (Grube et al.)
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) with Institute of Legal Medicine, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
sources.title: A Mobile Robotic Approach to Autonomous Surface Scanning in Legal Medicine
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator with an RGB-D camera autonomously navigated and performed full-body surface scans of actual corpses in a legal medicine (autopsy) environment, achieving 92.45% average surface coverage; the authors note that fixed floor/ceiling-mounted robots such as Virtobot require a dedicated room, motivating the mobile approach.
sources.transferJustification: Same object and purpose as the morgue documentation instance (digital external documentation of a corpse), but a research prototype with partial coverage that does not document clothing, personal effects or produce the investigator's narrative record.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan is a commercially available autonomous drone scanning capability used by police agencies (e.g., Boston Police crime scene response) for crime and crash scene reconstruction: after an operator sets the scan volume, the drone flies and captures the photoset autonomously for photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of the scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (outdoor crime/crash scene photogrammetric documentation) shows autonomous capture of scene geometry and object positions, but it does not examine or record a decedent's condition (lividity, rigor, temperature, wounds under clothing) and does not produce the investigator's findings, so it does not complete the coroner instance.

tasks.label: Provide information concerning the circumstances of death to relatives of the deceased.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Remove or supervise removal of bodies from death scenes, using the proper equipment and supplies, and arrange for transportation to morgues.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Death in a private residence (unattended natural death, overdose, or suicide): coroner/deputy documents the body in situ on a bed, floor, bathroom or stairwell of a cluttered home, checks for personal effects and medications, then bags, tags, and lifts the decedent (often 150-300 lb dead weight) onto a cot with the removal service and rolls it out through narrow doors and porch steps into the transport van.

Death in a nursing home, hospice, or hospital falling under coroner jurisdiction: body in a bed or on a room floor in a licensed facility with staff, wide corridors, and elevators; coroner views and photographs the body, confirms ID band, supervises transfer to a covered cot, and dispatches it to the coroner's morgue or releases it to a funeral home.

Motor-vehicle crash on a roadway or highway shoulder: body entangled in wreckage or thrown from the vehicle, night/weather/traffic conditions, fluids and glass present; coroner coordinates with fire/extrication and law enforcement, keeps evidence intact, then bags and removes the decedent (sometimes fragmented remains) onto a cot for transport.

Outdoor or remote scene taken as found: field, woods, ditch, riverbank or water recovery, homeless encampment, farm, or construction site; often decomposed, burned, or skeletal remains requiring collection of the body plus surrounding material, carry-out over uneven ground with no vehicle access, and transport arrangement.

Death inside a controlled institutional or industrial premises (factory floor, warehouse, jail cell, or workplace): scene secured by the employer or corrections staff, machinery locked out; coroner documents position, supervises release from equipment or a confined space, and directs bagging, cot transfer, and transport to the morgue.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: The most capable human-lifting robot of record, RIKEN/Sumitomo Riko's ROBEAR, is an experimental platform that lifts a cooperative living patient from a bed with caregiver-directed control; it has never been shown handling a deceased, uncooperative body, bagging it, or moving it out of a building.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient transfer (lifting a whole human body from a bed). It is the closest robotic analogue to body removal, but the demonstration involves a cooperative living patient in a laboratory/mock care room under operator direction, so it does not substantiate autonomous handling of dead weight at a death scene.

sources.developer: Robot Intelligence Lab, Imperial College London (Kormushev et al.)
sources.title: ResQbot 2.0: An Improved Design of a Mobile Rescue Robot with an Inflatable Neck Securing Device for Safe Casualty Extraction
sources.claim: Stretcher-type casualty-extraction robots designed to load a whole human body onto themselves remain research prototypes validated only in physics simulation, not in real scenes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: casualty extraction (loading a supine human body onto a stretcher robot and moving it away from a scene) — mechanically the same problem as body removal, but validation is simulation-only, so it supports no positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Autonomous Casualty Extraction (ACE): HDMS arms on FLIR Kobra UGV with Casualty Transport Device
sources.developer: RE2 Robotics (with TATRC / US Army, FLIR Systems)
sources.title: RE2 Robotics to Develop Autonomous Casualty Extraction UGV Manipulator Arms for US Army
sources.claim: US Army-funded autonomous casualty extraction work uses a UGV with dual manipulator arms and a drag sled to pull a casualty to safety; it is a development program rather than a fielded system that lifts, bags, and loads bodies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic extraction of an incapacitated human body from an uncontrolled scene. It is the closest funded effort to autonomous body removal, but reporting describes an R&D award and prototype hardware, not demonstrated end-to-end autonomous extraction at worker quality.

sources.system: Lastel automated corpse storage and retrieval system
sources.title: Japan's death industry reaps grim profits
sources.claim: The only deployed automation that routinely moves human remains is purpose-built materials handling inside a dedicated facility: Lastel's automated storage system conveys already-coffined bodies between refrigerated racks and viewing-room hatches; it does not pick up, bag, or lift a body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized conveyance of human remains in a purpose-built facility. It shows machine handling of remains only when they are already coffined and fixtured on a rack, so it does not transfer to removing an unfixtured body from a death scene, even under the E1 counterfactual, which still requires bagging, cot transfer, and vehicle loading.

sources.title: Stryker Power-LOAD Cot Fastener System - 6390
sources.claim: Commercially deployed body-handling equipment used by removal services and morgues is powered lift-assist under continuous operator control, not autonomous robotics: the Power-LOAD system raises and loads an occupied cot into the ambulance but a human must transfer the body onto the cot and steer it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading a loaded cot into a transport vehicle, one sub-step of body removal. It is operator-actuated and covers only the vehicle-loading step, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

tasks.label: Inquire into the cause, manner, and circumstances of human deaths and establish the identities of deceased persons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reported death of a hospitalized, hospice, or nursing-home patient with a known medical history: the coroner/deputy takes the report, reviews the medical chart, phones the attending physician and next of kin, confirms identity from hospital records and family, decides no autopsy is needed, and rules cause and manner natural. Occurs in the coroner's office and on the ward; mostly records, phone calls and judgment.

Unattended death of an elderly or chronically ill person found at a private residence: the investigator drives out, examines the body in place (rigor, livor, injuries, needle marks), rolls and photographs it, inventories medicine bottles and the living conditions, interviews family, EMS and police, confirms identity from documents and relatives, releases the body to a funeral home, and certifies a natural or accidental death. Cluttered, uncontrolled home; pets, grieving relatives, decomposition odors.

Suspected overdose or suicide in a residence, motel room, or public place: joint scene work with police, external examination of the body, collection of paraphernalia, notes and medications, next-of-kin notification, transport to the morgue, ordering autopsy and toxicology, then integrating lab and police findings weeks later into a cause and manner determination.

Sudden traumatic death outdoors: highway crash, fall from height, farm or industrial accident. Night, weather, ongoing extrication or rescue, possibly entrapped or fragmented remains; the investigator documents body position and injuries, works with crash reconstruction and OSHA/police, identifies the decedent from a wallet, vehicle records or prints, and determines an accidental manner.

Morgue and autopsy-suite work: attend or direct the autopsy of a homicide or unexplained death, perform or witness the external examination, collect specimens and postmortem prints, review radiographs, histology and toxicology, reconcile them with the scene investigation, and sign out cause and manner.

Unidentified, decomposed, burned, or skeletal remains found in a field, woods, water, or fire scene: coordinate recovery of scattered remains, engage anthropology, odontology and DNA consultants, run AFIS/NamUs comparisons, and establish identity plus a cause of death where one can be determined.

sources.system: Mobile robotic surface-scanning system (Grube et al., TUHH / UKE Institute of Legal Medicine)
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology (Institute of Medical Technology and Intelligent Systems) with UKE Institute of Legal Medicine
sources.title: A Mobile Robotic Approach to Autonomous Surface Scanning in Legal Medicine
sources.claim: A mobile robot developed with the Institute of Legal Medicine at UMC Hamburg-Eppendorf autonomously plans viewpoints and performs full-body RGB-D surface scanning of actual corpses inside a legal-medicine facility, i.e. it automates external documentation only, not the medicolegal inquiry or the cause/manner determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: external documentation of the decedent, a sub-step of the coroner's examination. It substantiates only that a robot can image a body lying on a table in a controlled morgue room; it produces no cause, manner, circumstances, or identity finding, and was not shown at a death scene.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0, an industrial six-axis robot installed in the CT suite of the Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich, performs automated 3D surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement for post-mortem tissue and fluid sampling on bodies presented on the scanner table.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: specimen collection and body documentation during a minimally invasive autopsy. Transfer is limited: the robot works only on a body fixtured on a CT table in a purpose-built suite and performs sampling steps; the diagnostic interpretation, scene reconstruction and certification of cause and manner remain with forensic pathologists.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Semiautomated robotic, CT-guided needle placement for postmortem CSF sampling – a Novel application of the Virtobot
sources.claim: A further Virtobot application performs semiautomated, CT-guided lumbar and suboccipital needle placement for postmortem CSF ... in the forensic institute, again a sampling sub-step under pathologist supervision rather than an independent determination of cause of death.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: postmortem specimen acquisition. It shows robots participating in laboratory sampling in a fixtured setting, but the system is explicitly semiautomated and yields samples, not an inquiry into cause, manner, circumstances, or identity.

sources.system: AUV prototype for underwater crime scene investigation
sources.developer: University of Bath / partners (Rymansaib et al., Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response
sources.claim: An autonomous underwater vehicle prototype for underwater crime-scene work detected a submerged body as an anomaly during autonomous searches, i.e. robots can locate remains in the field but the reported capability stops at detection and imaging, not examination of the body or determination of how the person died.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: search and location of human remains at an outdoor scene. It bears on the recovery instance only; the system provides a detection cue for human divers and performs no external examination, evidence interpretation, identification, or cause-of-death finding.

tasks.label: Observe, record, and preserve any objects or personal property related to deaths, including objects such as medication containers and suicide notes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unattended death in a private residence (natural death, overdose, or suicide): the investigator walks a cluttered home, spots and photographs medication containers on nightstands and in bathroom cabinets, a suicide note, drug paraphernalia and syringes; records their position relative to the body, then collects, bags, seals, labels and transports them with a chain-of-custody log.

Death in a hospital, hospice, nursing home or other licensed facility: investigator works a standardized patient room, notes and photographs IV lines, infusion bags, medication cups and bottles, patient belongings in the bedside locker, collects relevant medication containers and personal effects, secures and logs them.

Outdoor or vehicle scene (roadway crash, park, alley, jobsite): investigator works alongside police in weather and traffic, locates and photographs a wallet, phone, pill bottles in a glovebox or scattered items near the body, recovers and packages them, and documents their location before removal.

Property intake at the coroner/medical examiner office or morgue: decedent's personal effects (clothing removed at intake, jewelry, wallet, cash, phone, prescription bottles) are photographed, described item by item on a property inventory, sealed into numbered property bags, logged into the evidence/property system, stored in a secure locker and later released to next of kin or law enforcement.

Scenes or intakes dominated by hazardous or contaminated property: a firearm that must be handled and made safe, loose sharps and used syringes, blood-soaked or wet clothing, badly decomposed remains with soiled effects, requiring careful handling to preserve trace evidence without contamination or injury.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products of widely varying shape and size (the kind of small consumer objects a coroner's property intake handles: bottles, phones, boxed goods) inside a purpose-built fulfillment cell, and has been rolled out beyond pilot sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-based singulation of diverse individual items in e-commerce. It transfers to the physical collection step of this task because the objects (pill vials, phones, wallets, packaged goods) are of comparable size, weight and grasp difficulty, and the identification-then-grasp-into-a-container cycle is the same as placing a recovered object into an evidence container, when the items are presented to the machine as a purpose-built cell would present them.

sources.system: Amazon automated made-to-fit paper bag and box machines
sources.date: 2025-05-07 (rollout announcement; machines in fulfilment centres since 2023)
sources.title: Amazon to deploy automated packaging machines across Europe, reducing waste for millions of customer orders
sources.claim: Amazon's automated packaging machines take an item placed into them, sense its dimensions, form and heat-seal a made-to-fit paper bag around it, and (in the box variant) apply the identifying label directly — the package-seal-label step of preserving an object, done automatically at deployed scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand packaging and labelling of individual retail items. It transfers because 'preserving' an object here means sealing it into a right-sized bag and applying an identifying label; the machine performs exactly that sequence, on items handed to it, in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: ScriptPro SP-line / CRS robotic prescription dispensing systems
sources.title: ScriptPro Robotic Prescription Dispensing Systems
sources.claim: ScriptPro robotic dispensing systems handle medication containers end-to-end in pharmacies: the robotic arm fills vials, automatically applies the prescription label with drug image and description, presents them, and logs the transaction with audit reports, at ~99.5% uptime and 99.7% counting accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and labelling of prescription vials. It transfers to the medication-container portion of this task — identical objects (pill vials of many dram sizes), the same requirement to attach an accurate identifying label and produce an auditable record — within a purpose-built machine enclosure at the pharmacy counter.

sources.title: cobas p 512 pre-analytical system (LCP1)
sources.claim: Roche's cobas p 512 is a fully automatic pre-analytical system that registers, decaps, sorts, recaps, seals and archives barcoded specimen containers under unbroken identity tracking in clinical laboratories — the machine analogue of logging and preserving physical items with a custody record.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated specimen registration, sorting and archiving. It transfers to the record-and-preserve half of this task because the machine takes custody of physical containers, registers each to an identity, and stores them with a complete electronic trail — the same requirement as an item-by-item property inventory with chain of custody — but only for containers presented to it in a purpose-built system.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi performs commercial autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals — picking supply items out of supply closets and ..., transporting lab specimens — but it fetches known, catalogued supplies from known locations rather than searching a room for arbitrary objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fetch-and-deliver mobile manipulation in a structured human facility (E2). It marks the frontier of what robots do unattended in hospitals and shows the gap: Moxi retrieves pre-identified stock items from fixed storage, and nothing in its deployment covers searching a room for unknown objects, documenting them in place, or packaging them to evidentiary standard.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: The leading home humanoid intended for household object handling, 1X's NEO, still depends on scheduled human teleoperation for most useful work in real homes rather than autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general object handling and tidying in private homes (E3). Because the most advanced fielded home manipulator relies on remote human operators, there is no autonomous system that could search a residence, recognize which objects relate to a death, and collect them at worker quality.

tasks.label: Arrange for the next of kin to be notified of deaths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Locate and document information regarding the next of kin, including their relationship to the deceased and the status of notification attempts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Collect and document any pertinent medical history information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inventory personal effects recovered from bodies, such as jewelry or wallets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intake at the coroner/medical examiner facility: a body arrives clothed and bagged from a scene. The deputy coroner/technician undresses the decedent, searches pockets, works rings off fingers, unclasps necklaces/watches, and lists, photographs, bags and seals each item into a property envelope with a chain-of-custody log.

Property already separated from the body (arrives in a bag from hospital staff, EMS or police, or was removed earlier). In the office the coroner spreads the loose items on a tray, identifies and describes each (ring, watch, phone, keys, cash), photographs them, counts them, places them in a numbered property envelope, seals and labels it, and enters the list into the case record.

Wallet/purse contents inventory: opening a bifold wallet or handbag, extracting and counting currency, listing credit cards, ID cards and papers individually, re-securing them, and recording the itemized count for the valuables log (money is often counted and witnessed by a second person).

At the death scene — private residence, roadside, hotel room, wooded area, or public sidewalk — the deputy coroner searches the body for ID and valuables, removes and lists jewelry, wallet and phone, packages them, and documents them in the scene report before the body is moved.

Decomposed, burned, submerged or heavily traumatized remains: effects are soiled, fused to tissue or clothing, or fragmented; items must be gently separated, hazard-handled, air-dried or cleaned, photographed, described and logged, often with biohazard precautions.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics™ | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomously picks individual small, diverse items from mixed-SKU totes, identifies them by barcode, and places them into designated order containers in commercial fulfillment installations — the same physical acts as separating loose personal effects and placing each into a labeled property container at a fixtured station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic each-picking and containerization of small varied goods. Transfers to cataloging loose personal effects (rings, watches, phones, keys) because objects are of comparable size/fragility, the required precision is pick-and-place into a container, and the work is presented in totes at a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products

instances.label: Pre-bid walkthrough of an existing occupied institutional or commercial building (school, hospital, office tower, warehouse) for a renovation/fit-out or MEP estimate: record truck/loading access and staging, existing electrical service and panel capacity, water/gas/sewer service entrances, roof and site drainage, floor levels and ceiling heights. Escorted visit, standard building, fixed layout.

Visit to an active construction site (building or heavy/civil) mid-project or at a pre-bid walk: mud, trenches, moving equipment and crews, partially built structure. Record haul-road and gate access, laydown area, site grading and drainage/dewatering conditions, temporary power/water and the location of permanent service connections.

Visit to an undeveloped greenfield parcel or raw land for a site-development or earthwork bid: walk the terrain, note slopes, ponding and drainage courses, vegetation and rock outcrops, approach road width and turning radii, and how far power, water, sewer and gas mains lie from the property line.

Visit to a private residential or small commercial property (home addition, driveway, septic/sewer connection, small remodel): assess equipment access around the house and through gates, yard grade and drainage away from the foundation, and the existing service entrance, meter, panel and cleanout locations. Owner present; conditions taken as found.

Escorted visit to an industrial plant, utility yard or port/campus facility for a service or equipment-installation estimate: rigging and crane access routes, tie-in points for power, compressed air and water, containment and drainage around the work area. Institution controls premises and access.

sources.claim: Seegrid's autonomous pallet trucks and lift AMRs autonomously pick up palletized payloads from staging and deliver them to floor locations inside warehouses and manufacturing plants; the fleet has driven over 20 million autonomous miles in customer production facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless transport of palletized goods (including cased beverages and packaged food) from staging to designated floor locations. Same object class and precision as delivering pallets/cases of drinking water or packaged meals to a fixed break station.

sources.title: Seegrid Lift RS1 Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR)
sources.claim: Seegrid's Lift RS1 AMR autonomously picks up payloads from inbound staging and transports them to bulk, floor or endcap locations without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pallet pickup and drop at designated locations, which is the fixtured-presentation version of getting cased water or packaged meals from a supply point to where workers take them.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Introduces Relay2, The New High-Capacity Hotel Delivery Robot
sources.claim: Relay Robotics' delivery robots autonomously carry items from a front desk or kitchen to specific rooms inside hotels and healthcare buildings, with more than one million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point delivery of small consumables (water, food, toiletries) inside an institution-controlled building, comparable to ferrying supplies within a labor camp or packing shed; loading and unloading remain human actions.

sources.system: Chef Robotics ChefOS robotic food-assembly arm
sources.title: Chef Robotics | Physical AI for the food industry
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven robotic arms autonomously portion and assemble meals on food-manufacturing lines, deployed at more than a ... and having produced over 100 million servings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated preparation and portioning of packaged meals in a purpose-built production line. Transfers to the food-production half of providing crew meals when meals are made in a machine-built setting rather than hauled to a field.

sources.title: Bear Robotics and SoftBank join forces to mass produce Servi, foodservice robot
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously run food from kitchen to tables in restaurants, casinos and hospitality venues, with thousands of units in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of prepared meals to people in a structured facility. Comparable to distributing meals to a crew inside a cafeteria or break area; humans still load and unload the trays.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business - New Atlas
sources.claim: Somatic sells a robot-as-a-service that autonomously cleans and disinfects commercial building restrooms day to day, after an initial human-assisted mapping and VR teaching setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous servicing of fixed restrooms in a building. Bears on keeping sanitation facilities usable for workers in a facility, but it does not relocate units, restock consumables, or handle waste tanks as field sanitation service requires.

instances.label: Start-of-shift issue at the field: crew boss/contractor opens the crew truck or tool trailer parked on a dirt turnrow at dawn and hands out picking knives, pruning shears, harvest bags/buckets, sized gloves, hats and other PPE to 20-40 seasonal workers, keeping a rough count of who took what.

Mid-shift replacement/exchange in the field: a worker's shears break, a knife dulls, gloves tear, or a ladder is damaged; the contractor walks or drives to the tool stock, finds a replacement, swaps it out, and sets the damaged item aside for repair or sharpening.

End-of-shift collection at the field: gathering hand tools and PPE back from the crew at the row ends, counting them against the morning count, checking for damage/loss, and locking them in the trailer or truck box on uneven ground.

Staging at the contractor's yard, shop or the grower's equipment barn: pulling shears, knives, buckets, bags and PPE off shelves and out of bins, checking/cleaning/sharpening them, assembling the day's kit for each crew and loading it into the crew truck or trailer.

Restocking supply: receiving or picking up a case order of tools, gloves and PPE from an ag-supply dealer, unpacking, and putting the items away into labeled bins/shelves in the storage shed while updating inventory counts.

sources.system: Snap-on AutoCrib industrial vending (RoboCrib TX/VX/LX series)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product line commercial since the 1990s)
sources.title: Experience the AutoCrib Advantage | Snap-on AutoCrib
sources.claim: Snap-on AutoCrib industrial vending systems dispense hand tools, PPE and shop supplies directly to workers, who authenticate with an ID card or fingerprint to issue or ..., with the machine performing the recordkeeping a tool-crib attendant would do.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task — furnishing tools and PPE to employees for use and taking them back — carried out for industrial crews. Objects (knives, blades, shears, gloves, safety gear) and the required precision are comparable to a farm crew's issue, but the exchange happens inside the machine's own purpose-built dispensing enclosure rather than at a field turnrow.

sources.title: AutoCrib ® Industrial Vending Solutions | Tenaquip
sources.claim: AutoCrib RoboCrib dispensing machines hold and automatically dispense hundreds to thousands of distinct items, from cutting tools to safety supplies, and are installed at more than 20,000 industrial locations worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale and item breadth (tools, safety supplies, boxes) for automated tool furnishing; same task as the farm contractor's tool issue, performed in a purpose-built dispensing machine.

sources.title: VENDING CASE STUDY – MACHINERY MANUFACTURING (Fastenal)
sources.claim: Fastenal FAST vending machines are installed across manufacturing sites to dispense and track consumable PPE such as gloves and safety glasses to employees, reducing over-issue.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class — issuing gloves and PPE to workers and tracking usage per employee — which is a large share of what a farm labor contractor furnishes; the environment is the machine's own dispensing cabinet.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows individual, varied inventory items into and out of storage pods in operating fulfillment centers, handling roughly three-quarters of item types.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level put-away and retrieval of diverse small goods into fixed storage locations. This is the manipulation core of restocking a tool store and pulling items back out, with comparable object variety and grasp precision, performed in a fixtured, fenced robotic workcell.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously recognizes and picks individual products out of containers and places them into specific totes for order aggregation inside fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting/order assembly of diverse individual items into a container. That is the same manipulation as assembling a crew's tool kit from stock when the stock is presented in bins at a fixed station.

sources.title: Burro – Agri Automation
sources.claim: Burro's autonomous outdoor robots navigate farm rows, greenhouses and nurseries using computer vision and GPS, following workers and carrying payloads of produce, packing materials and ...; fleets of dozens are deployed commercially at growers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hauling materials to and from crews in open fields (E3). It shows autonomous field logistics is real, but the robot is a carrying platform — humans load it and workers self-serve; it does not select, hand out, count or take back individual tools.

instances.label: Pre-dawn crew haul: the contractor/crew leader drives a 12-15 passenger van or small bus from a labor camp or town pickup lot over rural two-lane highways and unpaved farm access lanes to a field or orchard, parks at the field edge, and tells the crew which block and rows to start in.

Intra-farm shuttling during the shift: moving crews (and ladders, bins, water) between blocks, fields, or ranches over unpaved farm lanes, through gates, across muddy or rutted headlands, in response to mid-shift reassignments by the grower.

Small-crew runs on paved roads: 3-8 workers taken in a pickup or minivan on paved county/town roads to nearby packing sheds, greenhouses, nurseries, or vineyards, often with several stops and pickups en route.

Long-haul transport: driving H-2A or migrant workers multi-hour distances by van or bus from employer housing, an airport, or a border crossing over interstates and state highways to a distant farm, with fuel and rest stops.

On-site direction without transport: workers arrive in their own cars at a field or shed; the contractor musters them at the field edge, checks the roster/head count, splits them into crews, walks them to assigned rows or blocks, and redirects them during the day.

sources.title: Taking riders further, safely with freeways - Waypoint: The official Waymo blog
sources.claim: Waymo runs a commercial driverless ride-hailing service carrying public passengers point-to-point on mapped public streets and, since November 2025, on freeways in the Bay Area, Phoenix and Los ..., after more than 100 million fully ....
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the transport half of this task - carrying people from a pickup point to a destination on roads - but demonstrated only inside validated, HD-mapped metro service areas with approved curbside stops, not on rural or unpaved farm routes.

sources.title: May Mobility Now Offers Autonomous Driverless Rides in Peachtree Corners, Georgia
sources.claim: May Mobility operates a commercial driver-out (nobody behind the wheel) autonomous passenger service in Peachtree Corners, GA, carrying public riders on demand between eight fixed stops along a business-park corridor, five passengers per vehicle.

sources.title: WeRide Launches Southeast Asia's First Fully Driverless Robobus Operations at Resorts World Sentosa, Singapore
sources.claim: WeRide runs a fully driverless Robobus with no safety officer aboard, carrying groups of public passengers on fixed internal routes inside the Resorts World Sentosa resort complex; tens of thousands of passengers were carried over a year of service.
sources.transferJustification: Group passenger shuttling between fixed points inside an institution-controlled facility is the same delivery-of-people-to-a-work-location act at crew-sized capacity.

sources.system: ATL Plane Train (Alstom Innovia automated people mover)
sources.title: The Plane Train: Getting You There Since 1980 - Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport
sources.claim: Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson's Plane Train is a fully automated, driverless people mover carrying a quarter million passengers a day between fixed stations on a dedicated guideway.
sources.transferJustification: Purpose-built (E1) analogue of moving a group of people to the correct destination: riders board at a platform and are delivered, unattended, to the station serving their work location.

sources.title: Kodiak AI Delivers Customer-Owned Autonomous RoboTrucks to Atlas Energy Solutions
sources.claim: Kodiak's driverless trucks, owned and operated by Atlas Energy Solutions, run with no one in the ... over a 21-mile off-road dirt lease-road route in the Permian Basin, hauling frac sand commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless vehicle transport of loads (not people) over unpaved private site roads at an operator-controlled industrial site; shows internal dirt haul roads are handled, though no passengers are carried.

sources.system: autonomous nursery shuttles (Sierra Gold Nurseries automation)
sources.developer: Sierra Gold Nurseries (vendor unnamed in article)
sources.title: Labor expenses push farmers to automate - Ag Alert
sources.claim: At Sierra Gold Nurseries, a 65-acre California nursery, autonomous shuttles move plants between growing areas in place of human-driven utility vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous vehicle runs between work areas inside a controlled agricultural facility carrying plants rather than workers; supports driverless intra-facility movement on farm-property roads.

sources.title: Aurora Launches Driverless Runs Between Fort Worth and El Paso - Dallas Innovates
sources.claim: Aurora operates fully driverless Class 8 trucks with no human on board on long intercity highway lanes in Texas, including a 600-mile Fort Worth-El Paso route.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-distance driverless highway operation carrying freight, not passengers; it shows highway driving over hundreds of rural miles but does not substantiate carrying a crew of workers.

instances.label: Pre-event walkthrough of a hotel ballroom or banquet room a few hours before doors open: planner walks the room with the banquet event order and floor diagram, verifying table count and spacing, chairs per round, linen and napkin color, head table and staging, dance floor, place cards and centerpieces, buffet/bar stations, podium and mic, screen/projector and lighting levels, room temperature, signage, and clear egress; discrepancies are flagged to the banquet captain for correction before guests arrive.

Pre-contract site inspection of a prospective venue (hotel, conference center, restaurant private room), usually escorted by a sales manager and sometimes with the client present: assess room capacities under different sets, ceiling height, columns and sightlines, power and rigging points, load-in doors and freight elevator, restrooms, ADA access, breakout adjacency, and noise from adjoining rooms; take photos and measurements and judge suitability against the client's program.

Inspection of a convention center exhibit hall and meeting rooms during move-in: walk the exhibit floor while crews, forklifts, and decorator staff work, checking aisle widths and booth positions against the floor plan, registration counters, hanging signage, fire-lane and egress compliance, breakout room sets, wifi/AV drops, and dock scheduling; issues are raised with the general service contractor and venue operations.

Inspection of a non-traditional or outdoor venue \, historic estate, park, warehouse, or private residence: check ground level and turf condition, tent staking and layout, generator/power runs and cable paths, restroom trailers, parking and guest arrival path, weather and lighting contingencies, kitchen/prep space, and safety hazards; conditions and layout differ at every site.

Mid-event checks during a multi-day meeting: periodic passes through general session and breakout rooms to confirm rooms were reset per spec between sessions (correct set style, chair counts, refreshed water and pads, cleared trash), that break stations are replenished to contract, AV is working, signage matches the current agenda, and temperature is comfortable; corrections are requested from venue staff in real time.

sources.title: Automated Inspections Made Simple | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot with Orbit performs repeatable autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, capturing sensor data at pre-taught inspection points (gauges, thermal, acoustic) along recorded routes — fixed-asset condition monitoring, not conformance checking of a novel room setup against a client specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds. Shows autonomous traversal and sensing inside a human work facility, but the inspection targets are pre-registered fixed assets with known expected readings, not a one-off event set judged against a banquet event order, so it does not carry over to conformance inspection of event facilities.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols office buildings on scheduled rounds, flagging environmental and security anomalies, with in-house remote specialists reviewing and taking control; the checks are generic facility/security anomalies, not verification of an event setup against customer requirements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled indoor facility checks in a structured human workplace. Demonstrates autonomous navigation and anomaly reporting in corridors and rooms, but the detections are learned baseline deviations (people, doors, environmental readings), not item-level comparison of furniture, linens, AV and signage to a bespoke client spec.

sources.title: Simbe Introduces Improved Tally 4.0 Shelf-Scanning Robot
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously scans store aisles and reports on-shelf availability, price accuracy and planogram compliance, and is deployed across grocery chains. It is the closest deployed analogue to 'does the physical arrangement match the spec', but is limited to barcoded packaged goods on fixed shelving scanned at close range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compliance auditing of a physical arrangement against a specification (planogram) inside a structured facility. Transfer fails on objects and criteria: shelf SKUs are catalogued, labelled and in fixed geometry, whereas a ballroom set involves uncatalogued furniture, linens, staging, AV function, lighting and temperature judged against a per-event document.

sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot with Field AI autonomy conducts job walks on active construction sites, feeding capture into BIM/digital twins for progress tracking and deviation analysis — spec-versus-as-built comparison in an unstructured setting, but restricted to building geometry and installed work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous walkthrough of an unstructured site with deviation analysis against a design model. It substantiates navigation and data capture on rough, changing ground, but the analysis compares fixed building elements to a BIM model and does not address tenting, power runs, guest flow, weather contingency or client-suitability judgments an event planner must render.

sources.developer: Vega et al., IEEE conference paper
sources.title: Service Robot Navigation and Computer Vision Application in a Banquet Hall Setting | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A research prototype surveyed a banquet hall with a small wheeled service robot, navigating to table edges and using OpenCV to count items and track ellipses on tables — the only on-point work found, covering only item counting at a table, at demo maturity.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting and intent (surveying an event room during setup), but the demonstrated function is an item count and ellipse tracker on a single table with a low-computation vision pipeline; it is a sub-step at demo maturity and does not deliver an accepted conformance verdict on a full room against customer requirements.

instances.label: Direct-mail fundraising appeal: fold personalized letters and match them with reply cards and business reply envelopes, stuff into outer envelopes, seal, label/meter and tray for mailing. Batches of a few hundred to several thousand, done in the nonprofit's office/workroom or sent to a lettershop.

Gala/golf-tournament gift or swag bags: fill 100-500 tote bags with an identical assortment of donated and sponsor items (mug, water bottle, snack bar, gift certificates, coupon flyers, program insert), sometimes with tissue paper, staged in the office or a storage room before the event.

Silent-auction paperwork: print and collate numbered bid sheets, pair each with an item description card and sponsor/valuation slip, mount on clipboards or in holders, and box them in item-number order ready for the auction tables.

Registration/check-in materials: variable-data printing of name badges, table assignment cards, donor packets, programs and pledge/gift envelopes; collating each guest's set and sorting finished sets alphabetically into check-in boxes.

Ad hoc, last-minute material prep in an uncontrolled space: a volunteer's home or garage, a church basement, or a back-of-house corner at the venue on event day - counting, collating, stuffing and boxing materials amid clutter and shifting layout.

tasks.label: Fill customer orders by packaging sold items and documentation for direct shipping or by transferring orders to manufacturers or third-party distributors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solo home-based merchant (Etsy/eBay/Shopify seller) fills the day's 5-50 orders from stock kept in a spare room, garage or basement: locate item in bins/shelves, wrap fragile goods, insert a printed packing slip and thank-you card, choose a poly mailer or reused box, tape it, print the label on a desktop thermal printer and apply it, stage for carrier pickup. Very high item variety, many one-off or handmade/resale SKUs.

Merchant with a small dedicated stockroom/warehouse and a few staff: batch-pick standard SKUs from shelving to a cart, pack at a bench using a few standard carton sizes and void fill, drop in packing slip/invoice and marketing insert, weigh, print-and-apply carrier label, sort to carrier bins. Dozens to a few hundred orders per day.

Larger online retailer operating its own fulfillment center with WMS, conveyors and pack stations: pick to tote, consolidate multi-item orders, right-size carton or bag, insert invoice/packing documentation, seal, weigh, label, manifest and sort to outbound trailer. Thousands of orders per day, standardized processes.

Order is not handled physically at all: the merchant transfers it to the manufacturer, dropship supplier or third-party distributor — forwarding order and address data by app/API/EDI/FTP or email, cutting a purchase order, and passing shipping documentation back to the customer. Purely informational work done at a desk.

Special-handling physical orders: fragile or oversized goods needing protective packing, multi-item bundles/kits assembled to order, perishables with cold packs, and international shipments requiring customs declarations and commercial invoices attached to the parcel.

Presentation-critical orders: gift wrapping to a customer's request, ribbon/tissue 'unboxing experience', handwritten personal note or gift message, custom arrangement of items in the box for photograph-worthy presentation.

instances.label: Replenishment/new-goods buying from online suppliers: researching wholesale catalogs and marketplaces (Alibaba, Faire, distributor B2B portals), comparing landed cost against marketplace sell-through data, negotiating terms by email/chat, and placing and paying for a purchase order that the supplier ships in. Done at a desk; no goods are handled by the merchant at purchase time.

Online bidding/buying of used or returned goods in bulk: customer-return pallets and shelf-pull lots on B-Stock, Liquidation.com, GovDeals or online estate/consignment auctions. Merchant reviews manifests and photos, sets a maximum bid, wins the lot, pays, and books freight or a will-call pickup slot.

Retail arbitrage run: driving to big-box and clearance retailers (Walmart, Target, TJX, Costco, drugstores), walking aisles and endcaps, barcode-scanning candidates against a sales-rank/profit app, judging quantity limits and condition of open-box items, filling carts, paying at the register, and loading the vehicle.

Used-goods sourcing inside secondhand retail: thrift chains, charity shops, consignment stores and 'bins' outlets. Merchant digs through racks and unsorted bins, inspects garments and hard goods for stains, tears, authenticity marks, missing parts and function, comps prices on a phone, then buys at the counter and hauls the haul out.

Private and casual physical sources: garage sales, estate sales, flea markets, church/school sales and Facebook Marketplace/Craigslist meetups. Unpredictable layout and inventory, cash haggling with individuals, on-the-spot authentication of collectibles or electronics, and lifting/transporting bulky items from a stranger's home or driveway.

Buyback intake channel: acquiring used consumer electronics or similar graded goods directly from individual sellers who bring or ship the item to the merchant. Merchant identifies the model, tests function and cosmetic condition, checks ownership/blacklist status, offers a price, pays on the spot, and takes custody for resale on a retail or auction site.

sources.claim: The ecoATM kiosk machine performs the whole purchase transaction for used devices at more than 7,000 US host stores: the consumer plugs the device in, the kiosk photographs and validates it, reads the IMEI against a lost/stolen database, makes a price offer and dispenses cash; devices are then resold, including through the company's own pre-owned retail site Gazelle. Human staff only remotely verify ID selfies.

instances.label: Home-based solo online merchant (garage, spare bedroom, basement): keeps an assorted stock of flat cartons, poly mailers, tape rolls, bubble wrap, void fill and label rolls on household shelving and in floor piles; eyeballs levels while packing orders, notes what is running low, receives supply cartons at the door, breaks them down, stacks flats and refills the packing table; places reorders online.

Small leased commercial unit or store backroom with 1-5 packers: metal shelving, two packing benches, standard carton sizes; weekly walk-through count of each carton size, tape, dunnage and labels; pulls cases from bulk shelving to replenish the benches; receives parcels or a pallet of supplies, checks against the packing slip and puts them away; updates a spreadsheet and reorders.

Mid-size e-commerce fulfillment center or 3PL: packaging consumables managed in a WMS with min/max reorder points; cycle counts of corrugate, dunnage and label stock in racking; pallets of supplies received at the dock, verified and put away into reserve locations; consumables fed to pack stations; supervisor spot-checks accuracy.

Overflow / offsite supply storage: bulk cases of boxes and bubble wrap kept in a rented self-storage unit, garage loft or van; merchant drives over, counts what remains, hauls cases back to the packing area, and keeps a running tally across two uncontrolled locations.

Point-of-use replenishment during a peak shipping day inside the fulfillment space: a packer runs out of a carton size or tape mid-shift; someone fetches a bundle from bulk storage, cuts it open, restocks the bench and dispensers, and flags the item for immediate reorder.

instances.label: Comprehensive physical security survey/audit walk-through of a corporate office building or campus: examine perimeter doors and hardware, locks and key control, card readers, turnstiles, lobby screening, CCTV placement and coverage, lighting, signage and barriers; sample-test doors/readers; photograph deficiencies; judge each against corporate standards, ASIS guidance and local code; produce an accepted findings-and-recommendations report.

Inspection of a regulated or classified secure area (SCIF, vault, evidence room, data-center cage, DEA/pharmacy area): close physical examination of door and lock hardware (e.g., GSA/X-09), hinges, walls and penetrations, IDS devices and tamper seals, container records, acoustic protection; compare against ICD 705 / 32 CFR / PCI requirements; complete the formal inspection checklist and certification write-up.

Post-installation acceptance inspection at a construction or fit-out site: verify newly installed cameras, readers, door contacts, intrusion sensors, gates, bollards and cabling against approved drawings and specs; check mounting, aiming, labeling and code compliance; functionally test each device with the integrator; issue punch list and sign-off.

Outdoor perimeter and critical-infrastructure compliance inspection at a plant, port, substation or logistics yard: walk/drive the fence line and gates, check fabric, fasteners, clear zones, vehicle barriers, guard booths and gate operators; take illumination readings with a light meter; verify camera fields of view and detection coverage; document deficiencies against regulatory standards, in weather and rough terrain.

Rapid checklist inspections across multiple small sites (bank branches, retail stores, clinics, schools) during business hours: confirm required devices are installed and operational, check alarms/panic buttons, safes and cash controls, door hardware and egress, key control records; interview site staff; file standardized compliance scorecards per site.

Scheduled recurring internal compliance round at a single enterprise facility: traverse the building on a set route to verify access-controlled and restricted-area doors are secured and not propped, that restricted spaces are clear after hours, and that no obvious environmental or security anomalies exist; log exceptions and time-stamped evidence into the facility's compliance record.

tasks.label: Conduct security audits to identify potential vulnerabilities related to physical security or staff safety.

instances.label: Comprehensive walkthrough security audit of a corporate office or multi-tenant building: physically test perimeter doors, locks, closers and panic hardware, check badge readers and turnstiles, look for camera blind spots and obstructions, inspect server/telecom rooms and stairwells, verify visitor management and key control, interview facility and reception staff, then deliver a prioritized findings-and-recommendations report.

Recurring checklist condition inspection of a fixed industrial/warehouse or logistics campus perimeter on a known route: confirm gates and roll-up doors are secured, fence line intact, exterior lighting operating, cameras unobstructed, no debris or vehicles creating access aids; log each checkpoint with photos and flag exceptions.

First-time or annual vulnerability survey of the same class of industrial/warehouse site: map adversary approach paths, judge fence height/climb aids, measure night lighting levels, evaluate camera coverage geometry and loading-dock exposure, assess guard post placement, and write an assessment with graded risk ratings and mitigation recommendations.

Physical penetration test / covert entry engagement at a client facility: attempt tailgating at employee entrances, test badge cloning and lock or latch bypass, probe after-hours doors and delivery entrances, social-engineer reception, document how far access was obtained and debrief the client.

Compliance-driven audit of a regulated or high-security area (data center cage, hospital pharmacy and ED, bank branch vault, school, utility substation): test duress/panic buttons and alarms, verify locks and key/core control, pull and reconcile access-control logs against authorized rosters, check restricted-area signage and mantraps, complete a standardized audit form for the regulator or insurer.

Staff-safety and workplace-violence risk assessment: observe reception and cash-handling workflows, evaluate lone-worker and late-shift exposure, walk egress routes and parking access, interview employees about incidents and concerns, review incident/injury data, and recommend administrative and physical controls.

tasks.label: Test security measures for final acceptance and implement or provide procedures for ongoing monitoring and evaluation of the measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final acceptance (commissioning) testing of a newly installed or upgraded electronic security system in an occupied corporate office building or campus: run the documented test script at dozens of card-reader doors and devices (valid/invalid credential, door-forced-open, door-held-open, request-to-exit, egress hardware, intrusion zones), confirm each event annunciates and logs correctly at the head end with the right camera call-up, check labeling and as-builts, record deficiencies on a punch list, retest, sign the acceptance certificate and hand over the periodic re-test schedule.

Site acceptance and performance testing of perimeter and outdoor measures at an institution-controlled industrial or critical-infrastructure site (substation, chemical plant, water utility, data center, port): conduct intrusion trials against each detection zone (climb-over, crawl-under, fence cut), test gates, barriers, turnstiles and duress devices, measure lighting levels, verify night-time camera assessment, alarm annunciation in the SOC and officer response, and document pass/fail with remediation actions.

Testing measures at small, distributed or unstructured sites taken as found: retail or bank branch, school, construction-site or temporary event perimeter, remote unmanned station. Verify duress/panic buttons ring the central station, test open/close signaling and alarm transmission, check locks, safes, gates and camera views, and confirm on-site staff can execute the response procedure; layout and conditions differ at every site.

Adversarial validation of the measures and of guard-force procedures at a client facility: after-hours entry attempts, tailgating/piggybacking, credential cloning, probing unsecured openings, timing officer response and post-order compliance, then debriefing management and issuing a corrective-action plan.

Implementing the ongoing monitoring and evaluation program after acceptance: writing test-and-inspection SOPs and recurring test schedules, configuring KPI reporting/dashboards from the access control and video systems, briefing and training the guard force and facility staff on the procedures, and running the first periodic review of results to adjust the program. Work occurs in client offices and the security control room.

instances.label: Routine walk-through inspection of the installed physical security system inside a corporate or institutional building (office, hospital, warehouse, data center): verify cameras present, aimed and unobstructed; sensors, readers and keypads undamaged and untampered; doors secured; lighting adequate; alarm/access panels showing normal status; log deficiencies.

Fire-safety walk-through inspection of a facility: extinguishers present, accessible, pin/seal intact and pressure gauge in the green; exit routes, exit signs and sprinkler heads unobstructed; fire alarm panel indicators normal (no trouble/supervisory); note and report deficiencies.

Exterior/perimeter security inspection at an employer- or client-controlled site (industrial plant, substation, distribution yard, data center campus): fence line and gate integrity, vehicle barriers, exterior camera and lighting condition, signage, sensor poles; often at night or in weather.

Functional testing/verification of intrusion detection and access control: walk-test motion detectors, trip door/window contacts and glass-breaks, press duress buttons, present test credentials at card readers, confirm each zone annunciates at the panel and transmits to the central station, test sirens and REX/door-held alarms.

Functional testing of fire detection/suppression devices: aerosol/heat test smoke and heat detectors (including high ceilings), activate pull stations, verify notification appliances, check sprinkler control valves and tamper/flow switches, verify extinguisher service tags, then silence and reset the panel.

Inspection at varied, unstructured sites: an active construction site or temporary facility with a portable alarm/camera kit, a small leased satellite office or strip-mall retail unit, or an executive residence 
ovter and novel obstacles present, layout differs site to site, no institutional standard for the premises.

instances.label: Install or replace video surveillance devices at an employer's facility: mount cameras/housings to ceilings, walls, soffits or parking-lot poles from a ladder or lift, drill and anchor, route and fish cable above ceilings/through conduit to the IDF, terminate/land it on a PoE switch or NVR, then aim, focus and verify field of view against the design.

Install or retrofit electronic access control at a door opening: mount card reader, electric strike or maglock, request-to-exit sensor and door position contact; drill/route the frame, pull and dress low-voltage cable to the controller cabinet, land conductors on controller and power-supply terminals, then test door release, alarms and fail-safe behavior.

Service call on a deployed system in an occupied facility: diagnose a dead camera, intermittent reader, nuisance intrusion alarm or failed door controller with a meter and laptop, trace wiring in closets and above ceilings, re-terminate loose conductors, swap a board, power supply or standby battery, and retest the affected devices back to the head end.

Commission and program on-site panels, controllers and PLCs: connect to the alarm/access panel or PLC, wire and verify field I/O to gates, turnstiles, bollards or barrier interlocks, load firmware and logic, set device addresses and zones, then walk-test every sensor and interlock with a partner and correct wiring/config faults found.

Security electronics work in unstructured settings: temporary construction-site cameras and trailer alarms, perimeter fence-mounted sensors and solar/wireless cameras at a remote utility or storage yard, or an executive's private residence — no standard layout, unknown existing wiring, weather and terrain taken as found.

Shop/bench prefabrication before field deployment: wire out a security control panel mounting plate to the ECAD drawing — cut, strip, ferrule and label conductors, route them in wire duct and land them on DIN-rail terminal blocks, relays, power supplies and controller I/O — for later installation at the site.

It transfers to shop prefabrication of a security control panel because the workpiece and objects are the same class (DIN-rail terminal blocks, relays, controller I/O, ferruled 0.75-2.5 mm2 conductors, wire duct), the precision required is terminal-screw/push-in level, and the plate is presented fixtured in a purpose-built machine cell exactly as the E1 counterfactual specifies.

sources.system: Automated control cabinet wiring cell (research prototype) / survey of Averex and comparable systems
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (SpringerLink)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed study of control-cabinet automation reports that automation exists only for individual production steps and that no purchasable, industry-proven system covers the complete cabinet build; the authors' own full-process solution is a lab prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain as the shop prefabrication instance; bounds how much of a panel build is automatable today and shows that field-style flexible wiring remains manual.

sources.title: Hilti's Robot Breaks Records on a YIT Construction Site - AEC Business
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot, the closest commercially deployed robot to in-building electrical/MEP installation, only drills BIM-specified ceiling holes and marks them; an operator drives it into position by remote control and a surveyor sets up the total station, and it does not mount devices, pull cable or terminate conductors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead anchor drilling for MEP/low-voltage installation in buildings — the sub-step closest to mounting security devices. It shows that even this narrow sub-step needs operator repositioning and surveyed markers, so it does not substantiate whole-instance device installation, cabling or termination.

sources.system: Figure 02/03, Agility Digit, Apptronik Apollo (industrial humanoid deployments)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots on Manufacturing Floors in 2026 (iFactory)
sources.claim: Across documented 2026 deployments, general-purpose humanoid and mobile-manipulator platforms in structured facilities are limited to material handling, parts transfer, bin ...; none are documented installing, servicing or repairing electronic security devices in occupied buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the scope of mobile manipulation deployed in E2 facilities; the demonstrated task set (tote and part handling) does not include ladder/lift work, cable pulling, or screw-terminal wiring, so it cannot substantiate this task.
