instances.label: Attending a distributor's / 3PL's physical inventory at a distribution center or third-party warehouse: walking racked aisles of labeled, palletized cartons, selecting sample locations, test-counting cartons/pallets, tracing counts both ways to count sheets and the perpetual (WMS/GL) records, and noting damaged or slow-moving stock.

Inventory observation at a retail store, warehouse club or supermarket: counting packaged goods on shelves, end caps and pallet stacks plus a backroom, checking unit-of-measure and price/SKU tags, and reconciling test counts to the store's perpetual inventory and ledger balance.

Raw-material stores and finished-goods area inside a manufacturing plant: racked, barcoded material and pallets in a plant warehouse, counted and reconciled to the ERP/inventory subledger, with observation of the client's count procedures and tag control.

Work-in-process on a factory shop floor: partially completed assemblies on lines, loose components in bins and totes, judging stage of completion and condition, matching to job/work-order records and the WIP ledger account.

Bulk and outdoor inventory at a mine, quarry, coal yard, grain or log yard, or tank farm: measuring or observing measurement of stockpile volumes/tank levels, converting to tonnage, and comparing to the recorded quantities in the inventory ledger.

Small or scattered client locations: a small retailer's or contractor's cluttered stockroom, shed, service vans, restaurant walk-ins, jewelry cases, or consigned goods at customers' sites - heterogeneous, often unlabeled items with no barcoding or perpetual system, counted and matched to handwritten/spreadsheet listings and the ledger.

sources.title: Maersk taps drones for warehouse inventory management | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones fly inside active Maersk warehouses, image SKUs on pallets and compare what they find against the warehouse management system's recorded inventory, flagging discrepancies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: client-side cycle counting reconciled to the perpetual record. Transfer: same objects (racked pallets/cartons), same precision (location-level quantity and label reads), same environment (an active warehouse), and the same output an auditor's test count produces - an independent physical count compared with recorded quantities, with exceptions listed.

sources.title: LAPP USA Case Study: Corvus One Inventory Drones - Corvus Robotics
sources.claim: Corvus One drones fly nightly, pilot-free missions through a 134,000 sq ft distribution warehouse, scanning thousands of pallet positions and producing pallet-validation and discrepancy reports with photo evidence of every position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cycle counting replacing five associates' weekend counts. Transfer: the system delivers exactly the physical evidence an inventory observation rests on - counted/validated pallet positions, discrepancy reports and retained photo evidence tied to the record.

sources.claim: Corvus states its infrastructure-free autonomous inventory drones operate continuously inside active warehouses ..., including sub-zero freezer warehouses, delivering cycle counts without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Extends the warehouse counting evidence to plant stores/finished-goods areas inside manufacturing facilities, which hold the same racked, labeled pallets counted in the audit instance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Transfer: item-level data capture (lot codes, expiry, counts) at accuracy levels (99.9%) at or above manual counting is the precision an auditor's test count requires, in the same warehouse setting.

sources.title: Simbe Robotics finding success counting inventory at BJs Wholesale Club - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Tally robots operate in the selling area of BJ's clubs during trading, imaging pallets and shelves and reconciling the observed inventory against the client's inventory system; Simbe's fleet spans roughly 1,000 stores.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: the physical count-and-reconcile step of a retail inventory observation, performed autonomously in an occupied store.

Transfer: the physical act an auditor performs on bulk inventory is exactly volumetric measurement of piles converted to tonnage for comparison with the ledger; accuracy of 1-3% matches or exceeds manual survey.

sources.title: Drones in audit - PwC case study
sources.claim: PwC UK reports that drone-based capture of independent volumetric data for stockpile audits, first flown in 2018 (including RWE coal stocks), is now an established audit methodology aligned to international auditing standards.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that machine-captured volumetric inventory data is accepted as audit evidence for verifying recorded stock quantities; flight autonomy is not established, so it is used only to establish acceptance of output quality, not autonomy.

instances.label: Jewelry/gemstone appraisal at a retail store back office, gem lab, or bank vault: appraiser gauges stone dimensions and estimated weight, examines color/clarity/cut and finish under loupe or microscope, weighs the piece, tests and records metal karatage, reads hallmarks, notes mounting design/style, and photographs the piece for the report.

Machinery & equipment appraisal at an operating factory, processing plant, or distribution facility: appraiser walks the floor asset by asset, records nameplate make/model/serial, capacity and overall dimensions, notes condition/wear/modifications, and photographs each machine for the asset schedule.

Fine art, antiques, collectibles and household contents at a private residence or estate: appraiser measures canvases, frames and furniture in situ, records maker's marks/signatures/labels, describes period, materials, design and construction, notes condition (losses, repairs, craquelure, wear), and photographs items where they sit amid furnishings.

Intake cataloguing at an auction house, gallery, or storage facility: consigned items are brought to a table or photo station where the appraiser measures and weighs them, records marks and design details, notes condition, and shoots catalog images.

Vehicles, trailers and heavy/yellow-iron equipment at a dealer lot, fleet yard, or contractor's yard: appraiser records VIN/serial and hour or odometer readings, measures body/attachment configurations, documents tires, glass, body damage and interior condition, and photographs each unit outdoors.

tasks.label: Inspect personal or business property.

instances.label: On-site inspection of household/estate contents in a private residence: appraiser walks through occupied rooms, handles paintings, ceramics, silver, furniture and rugs, checks backs of canvases, undersides, maker's marks, joinery, repairs and damage, measures and photographs each item, and records identification and condition notes for an estate or insurance appraisal. Clutter, pets, family present, no fixed layout.

Machinery & equipment inspection at an operating plant, warehouse, shop or contractor's yard: appraiser walks the floor with a client escort, locates each asset, reads nameplates for make/model/serial/capacity, notes hour meters, attachments, wear, missing guards, retrofits and operability, photographs each unit, and builds an asset list with condition ratings for a lending or liquidation appraisal.

Bench inspection of mounted jewelry, watches and holloware at a jeweler's office, bank vault room or appraiser's studio: unmounting is not permitted, so the appraiser weighs the piece, measures mounted stones with gauges, estimates grades under a loupe/microscope, tests and reads karat/hallmarks on the metal, checks prongs, solder repairs and wear, and photographs the piece.

Furniture, fixtures and equipment inventory at a business premises (office, restaurant, medical clinic, retail store): appraiser walks the leased space, counts and categorizes desks, casework, POS and kitchen equipment, IT gear and signage, records makes/models/ages and condition, and ties the inventory to the client's fixed-asset ledger.

Laboratory/bench inspection of loose diamonds and gemstones submitted for grading or valuation: stones are presented one at a time under controlled lighting; the inspector weighs, measures proportions, assigns cut/color/clarity grades, maps inclusions, checks fluorescence and natural vs. lab-grown, and outputs a grading record used for the value conclusion.

Inspection of a collectibles consignment at a dealer's shop or auction house intake room: mixed lots of coins, trading cards, stamps, sports memorabilia, toys and signed items are examined for authenticity marks, mint/condition grade, restoration and damage, then identified, photographed and catalogued.

instances.label: Jewelry, gemstones, coins and small collectibles photographed on a bench in the appraiser's office, a jeweler's back room, or a gem lab: overall views plus macro detail shots of hallmarks, maker's marks, inclusions, mountings and wear, with a scale reference, for insurance/estate appraisal reports.

Fine art, antiques, furniture, rugs, silver and decorative arts photographed in situ during an on-site inspection at a client's private residence or estate: full views of each item plus close-ups of signatures, labels, undersides, joints and condition problems, under whatever ambient light and clutter the rooms present.

Machinery and equipment photographed at an operating plant, shop, or contractor's yard: wide shot of each asset plus close-ups of nameplates/serial numbers, hour meters, attachments and damage, while production continues around the appraiser and PPE is required.

Business personal property (furniture, fixtures and equipment) photographed at commercial premises such as a restaurant, medical office, salon or retail storefront: kitchen line, exam rooms, display cases, back-of-house equipment, during or around business hours.

Bulk merchandise and stock-in-trade photographed inside a distribution center, wholesale warehouse or retail store: racked pallets, aisles of shelved goods, stacked cartons, documenting quantities and condition of the inventory being appraised.

Exterior/site photography of business property: building exteriors, equipment yards, storage lots and land parcels, including overhead/aerial views showing layout and the assets present, taken outdoors in variable weather and light.

tasks.label: Verify that property matches legal descriptions or certifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Loose diamond or colored stone submitted with a lab grading report (GIA/IGI/GCAL): at the appraiser's office or gem-lab bench, unpack the stone, weigh and measure it, check the laser inscription/report number under magnification, and confirm the stone's characteristics match the certificate before valuing it.

Fine art, antiques, collectibles, mounted jewelry and watches examined on site in a client's home, estate, gallery or the appraiser's office: compare the object to a certificate of authenticity, prior appraisal, hallmark, edition number, maker's mark, or case-back/movement serial, turning, lifting and opening the piece as needed, and judge whether the object is the one described.

Business inventory / stock-in-trade and tagged fixed assets in a warehouse or distribution center: walk (or count) the racked, labeled goods and asset-tagged items and reconcile what is physically present against ... inventory schedule or asset ledger supplied by the owner or lender.

Production machinery, shop and farm equipment at an operating plant, machine shop or yard, usually a first visit: locate each unit on the asset schedule / lien or title description, find the manufacturer nameplate (often greasy, low, behind guards or on the far side of the machine), read make, model, year and serial number, confirm configuration and attachments, and flag units that do not match or are missing.

Vehicles, trucks, trailers and heavy equipment on a dealership, auction, rental or fleet lot: match VIN/PIN plates and equipment serial numbers on each unit to titles, registrations and financing schedules, and confirm the unit's specification matches the documented description.

Land or improved real property: on the parcel, compare what is on the ground (improvements, acreage, access, encroachments) with the deed's legal description, plat or survey to confirm the property inspected is the property described.

tasks.label: Update appraisals when property has been improved, damaged, or has otherwise changed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Desk update of a scheduled personal-property appraisal (jewelry, art, collectibles) based on documentation the client or insurer supplies — repair invoices, restoration reports, claim photos, receipts for added stones or a new frame. The appraiser re-researches comparables, recalculates replacement value, and reissues the signed appraisal report and value schedule.

Jewelry/fine-art appraiser re-examines a specific item brought to the office or studio after reported damage (chipped diamond, dented setting, torn canvas, water staining), documents the condition change, then revises the existing appraisal's condition description and value and issues an updated report to the owner or insurer.

Machinery-and-equipment appraiser updates a business asset appraisal after a plant installs new equipment, rebuilds a machine, or suffers fire/flood loss: reconciles the fixed-asset list against capital-expenditure records, re-walks the facility, adjusts effective age/condition ratings, and reissues the updated valuation schedule and narrative.

Household contents/collectibles appraiser updates values after a loss event at a residence (fire, flood, burglary) — reconciles the prior inventory with what remains, records condition changes item by item, and produces the revised loss/value schedule for the insurance claim.

Periodic re-issuance of appraisal records for a fleet, collection, or leased-equipment portfolio: updating database entries and schedules to reflect reported additions, retirements, refurbishments, and damage, and delivering the amended appraisal documentation to the client.

instances.label: Full interior and exterior photo set for a lender appraisal of an occupied single-family home: the appraiser walks the furnished, sometimes cluttered house (stairs, basement, attic access, closets, garage), photographing every room, each bathroom, kitchen, mechanical systems, updates and deficiencies, then front/rear elevations and street scene, with occupants and pets present.

Exterior-only photography: drive-by / exterior-inspection appraisals and comparable-sales photos taken from the public street - front elevation, street scene, sometimes rear or side views from adjacent right-of-way, at several addresses in one trip, in whatever weather, parking and traffic conditions exist.

Interior photos of a condominium, townhouse or apartment unit in a multifamily building: entering through a managed lobby, corridor and elevator, photographing the unit's rooms and baths, plus common areas, amenities and the building exterior.

Commercial or industrial property: photographing an operating office suite, retail store, warehouse or small apartment building - interior spaces and tenant areas, building systems, plus exterior elevations, parking and site improvements, usually escorted by a property manager.

Assessor field work / mass appraisal: exterior photographs of many parcels on a reassessment route - houses, outbuildings, vacant lots, rural acreage and new construction - taken from the road or on foot at each parcel to document condition and improvements in the assessment record.

instances.label: Full interior-and-exterior inspection of an occupied single-family home for a mortgage appraisal (URAR 1004): walk every room of a furnished, cluttered house with stairs, closets, basement/crawlspace, attic hatch and garage; measure exterior perimeter/GLA to ANSI standard; photograph rooms, mechanicals and street scene; rate condition/quality and note updates and deferred maintenance; then develop and sign an opinion of value from comparable sales.

Exterior-only or 'drive-by' residential assignment (Form 2055), condo unit, or new-construction final inspection: observe the subject from the street or common areas, verify features, roof and site, photograph front and street scene, confirm completion, then complete the valuation.

County assessor field canvassing for mass appraisal: visit dozens of parcels per day in a neighborhood, measure or verify exterior dimensions, look for additions, pools, decks and new construction, rate condition and enter data into CAMA, working from public streets and private yards with fences, dogs and absent owners.

Commercial/income property inspection (office suite, retail strip, small industrial or multifamily building) escorted by a property manager: walk common areas, sample tenant spaces, roof and mechanical rooms, note construction type, condition, occupancy and deferred maintenance, gather rent roll data, then value via income and cost approaches.

Vacant land, rural/agricultural, or damaged/complex property: walk an unaddressed site over uneven ground to verify acreage, topography, access, utilities, outbuildings, crop/timber or fire/flood damage, often without maps or marked boundaries, then value the parcel.

sources.title: How to Use Drones for Roof Insurance Inspections
sources.claim: EagleView Assess uses a drone that, after an on-site operator outlines the scan area and launches it, autonomously plans its flight and captures full-coverage high-resolution imagery of a residential roof for insurance inspections; it covers only the roof/exterior and produces imagery and measurements, not a property value opinion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior roof/property inspection imagery for insurance adjusters. It is the closest robotic analogue to an appraiser's exterior observation of a dwelling, but it captures only roof facets from the air, does not enter or measure interiors, and delivers no condition/quality rating or opinion of value.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Leica BLK ARC (Autowalk reality capture)

It shows autonomous indoor traversal and 3D capture in industrial facilities, but requires a human-taught route per site, targets uncluttered industrial space rather than furnished homes, and yields a point cloud rather than an appraisal condition rating or value.

sources.title: Exyn Drones Achieve Autonomy Level 4: The Most Sophisticated Level of 3D Aerial Autonomy To-Date
sources.claim: Exyn's aerial robots are commercialized with mining, construction and logistics customers and can explore complex GPS-denied indoor spaces autonomously without a prior map, producing LiDAR scans; they are used for industrial volumetric mapping and inspection, not property valuation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous interior mapping of unknown GPS-denied spaces. It is the strongest evidence for map-free indoor autonomy, but deployments are large industrial voids (mines, shafts, warehouses), not occupied furnished dwellings, and the output is a point cloud with no condition assessment or value conclusion.

sources.system: Fannie Mae value acceptance + property data / hybrid appraisal (Uniform Property Dataset)

instances.label: County/municipal assessor field inspection of a newly completed single-family house on its lot, triggered by a building permit: locate the parcel, walk the exterior, measure footprint and stories, photograph, judge construction quality grade and finish materials, interview or knock for interior access where allowed, then enter characteristics into CAMA and set the assessed value.

Assessor inspection of a major improvement to an existing occupied home (room addition, finished basement, kitchen/bath remodel, garage, deck, pool): navigate an occupied, furnished dwelling with a homeowner present, verify what was actually built versus the permit, measure added area, judge quality and percent complete, and add the improvement's value to the roll.

Fee appraiser's inspection of a newly built home for a lender (new-construction appraisal or 1004D final inspection): walk interior and exterior, sketch and measure gross living area, photograph rooms, mechanicals and site, verify plans/specs and upgrades were completed, note condition/quality ratings, and reconcile to an opinion of value.

Inspection of new construction still in progress on an active construction site (house or small commercial building partially framed, muddy site, temporary stairs/ladders, trades working) to establish percent complete for a construction-loan draw or a partially-complete assessment as of the lien date.

Appraiser/assessor inspection of a newly built or substantially renovated commercial or multifamily property that is finished and operating: escorted walkthrough of lobby, representative units/suites, mechanical and roof areas, parking, verifying build-out quality and improvements for an income/cost-approach valuation.

sources.title: Drone Roof Inspections: Why to Use Them and How to Get Started
sources.claim: EagleView Assess is a commercially deployed drone system that flies an autonomous scan of a residential roof/property and produces imagery and AI-assisted damage assessment for insurers; an operator is on site to outline the scan area and launch, and the output covers only exterior roof surfaces, not interior walkthrough, living-area measurement, quality grading, or an opinion of value.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior roof/property condition capture for insurance claims. It shares the outdoor residential setting and photographic condition assessment of an appraiser's exterior inspection, but delivers only roof imagery and damage classification, so it cannot substantiate completion of a new-construction valuation inspection.

sources.title: Hastings Mutual Insurance Company and EagleView Assess: A Case Study for Successful Drone-Based Roof Claims
sources.claim: An insurer (Hastings Mutual) deployed EagleView Assess drones in production for roof claim inspections, confirming real-world commercial use of autonomous exterior scanning by trained operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: property exterior/roof condition documentation. Establishes maturity of autonomous exterior capture at residential properties, but the deliverable is a claims report, not a determination of value for new construction or improvements.

sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution for Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot, integrated with the Trimble X7 laser scanner and FieldLink, performs autonomous 3D scanning of construction sites along programmed routes for progress documentation; it is a commercial product used on active job sites, but it produces point clouds/digital-twin data rather than a valuation, and its missions must be pre-programmed for each site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction progress documentation by 3D scanning. It occurs in the same construction-site environment as a percent-complete inspection and captures dimensional data, but no evidence shows it judging construction quality, verifying permitted improvements, or producing an accepted value or percent-complete conclusion.

sources.title: Construction | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot for repeatable autonomous scanning missions on construction sites with autonomous charging via a dock, i.e. routine data collection along taught routes rather than one-off inspection of an unfamiliar property.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring site data capture. Shows the deployed mode is programmed repeat routes at a single managed site, which does not transfer to an appraiser's single visit to a never-before-seen property that must end in a value conclusion.

sources.developer: Mill Hill Garage / JB Real Estate Valuation & Advisory
sources.title: From Photons to Physics: Autonomous Indoor Drones and the Future of Objective Property Assessment
sources.claim: A 2025 review co-authored with a real estate valuation firm frames autonomous indoor drones for objective property assessment as a prospective paradigm shift still facing platform, sensing, and commercialization challenges, and describes current property inspection as a human appraiser walking through the home, measuring, photographing, and assigning ratings.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task context: it documents that interior property assessment remains human-performed and that autonomous indoor assessment drones are a research/commercialization prospect, supporting negative judgments rather than any positive one.

sources.claim: Fannie Mae's property data collection standard for hybrid and inspection-based valuation products requires a trained and vetted human third party to perform the full interior and exterior observation with a mobile app; no robotic collector is contemplated in the deployed workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the state of practice in lender-side inspection of homes: the industry's most automated variant still requires a human on site, confirming that no robotic system is accepted for the inspection step that precedes valuation.

instances.label: Routine residential field canvass: assessor drives assigned neighborhood routes in a jurisdiction, views each parcel from the street, and notes physical changes since the last review - new additions, decks, garages, pools, siding/roof replacement, or structures torn down - photographing and recording changes against the property record card/CAMA data.

Permit-triggered new-construction inspection: visit to a parcel with an open building permit (house under construction, addition, teardown/rebuild) to determine stage and percent complete as of the assessment date, measure the footprint of the new structure, note materials and quality, and photograph progress.

Verification visit for a flagged parcel: a change flagged by aerial/oblique imagery change-detection, a permit list, or a demolition record must be confirmed on the ground - assessor drives to the address, confirms whether the structure exists, was demolished, or was altered, and photographs backyard/rear structures not visible in the record.

Commercial, industrial, or multifamily property review: scheduled visit to an owner-controlled site (retail center, warehouse, apartment complex, plant) to check for renovations, tenant build-outs, expansions or partial demolition; access is coordinated with management/security, exterior walk-around plus occasional escorted interior look.

Rural or agricultural parcel review: long drives on county roads to scattered parcels, gated or unmarked access, checking for new outbuildings, barns, grain bins, mobile homes or collapsed/removed structures over large acreage with rough terrain and vegetation.

instances.label: Stationary residential stakeout: investigator parks an unmarked vehicle on a public street near a workers'-comp/disability claimant's home before dawn, sits covertly for 6-10 hours, identifies the subject on sight, and video-records them leaving the house, loading a truck, mowing, or driving - producing time-stamped evidentiary footage and a log/report.

Mobile follow: tailing the subject's vehicle through residential streets, highways and parking lots to gym, store, side job or medical appointment, staying undetected through traffic and losses, then re-establishing an observation post at each stop to film activity.

Foot/covert observation inside a public commercial venue (big-box store, gym, restaurant, sporting event): investigator blends in among patrons, keeps the subject in view amid crowds, and covertly records them lifting, bending, carrying, or working.

Fixed-post observation of a suspect business or worksite from a public vantage: documenting who and what enters a suspect clinic, pharmacy, body shop or contractor jobsite over days - counting arrivals, capturing license plates, and photographing a claimant performing work.

On-premises surveillance inside an institution-controlled facility (client's warehouse, retail store, hospital, casino, corporate campus and its lots): monitoring a suspect employee/provider area for internal theft, billing or premium fraud, using facility floor observation and covert/CCTV positions over days or weeks.

sources.title: How Autonomous Robots are Revolutionizing Public Safety
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol outdoor client premises (parking lots, corporate campuses, self-storage sites) continuously, recording 360-degree HD video, thermal and license-plate data without an operator driving them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = persistent security patrol/monitoring at a client site. It transfers to fixed-post fraud surveillance because the output is the same artifact: continuous, time-stamped, identifiable video and plate captures of who and what comes and goes at a designated location.

sources.title: Knightscope Security Robots Rack Up More Crime Fighting Wins
sources.claim: Evidence collected autonomously by deployed Knightscope robots has been handed to law-enforcement investigations, including a four-month monitoring assignment for a specific BOLO target that yielded HD video and 30 license-plate detections, and a case where robot-collected evidence alone elicited a confession.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = evidence-gathering for a criminal investigation by persistent robotic observation of a controlled site. Same objects (vehicles, plates, persons), same precision (identifiable imagery usable by investigators), same purpose (case-related information).

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt indoor security robots autonomously patrol interior facilities (offices, data centers, warehouses) around the clock, detecting anomalies and people and streaming/recording video that remote specialists review.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous indoor patrol and anomaly documentation in a human work facility; transfers to on-premises internal-fraud observation because it is the same setting, the same subjects (employees, doors, after-hours activity) and the same product (recorded video evidence plus event logs).

sources.title: Percepto Drone Regulation | BVLOS & Industrial Safety
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box autonomously launches from a dock at industrial sites and flies scheduled or event-triggered monitoring and security missions beyond visual line of sight, with FAA waivers permitting operation with no on-site personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = unattended aerial monitoring of a fixed industrial site. Transfers to fixed-post site observation (logging arrivals, imaging vehicles and yard activity) because the sensing task, standoff distances and imagery-quality requirements are comparable.

sources.system: Skydio X10 + Dock, 'Shadow' Track and Follow
sources.title: Skydio Dock for X10: Cayley 43.41.52 (Early Access) - 17 December 2025
sources.claim: Skydio X10 drones launched from a dock can autonomously identify, track and follow a designated person or vehicle with minimal ...; the feature shipped as an early-access/beta capability in December 2025 and runs under a remote pilot in command in BVLOS public-safety programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = aerial subject tracking, the closest analogue to mobile follow surveillance; but it is an overt, audible airborne platform with short endurance flown by a certificated remote pilot over pre-approved areas, so it does not establish covert multi-hour tailing of a claimant.

sources.title: Workers Compensation Surveillance Explained
sources.claim: Practitioners describe effective fraud surveillance as a judgment-driven investigative process rather than mechanical watching: the investigator studies the file, chooses vantage points and times, and often delivers value even when no activity footage results.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline description of the human task's acceptance standard; used only to characterize worker quality, not to support a positive robotic judgment.

sources.title: How Private Investigators Can Use Drones Legally for Surveillance
sources.claim: Private investigators using drones remain bound by FAA Part 107 and state privacy law, must avoid recording where subjects have a reasonable expectation of privacy, and risk harassment/stalking exposure from repeated aerial observation - constraints that block covert aerial stakeouts of residences.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative judgments on residential and mobile surveillance: the covertness and admissibility standard the worker's output must meet, which an overt aerial or wheeled robot cannot satisfy.

instances.label: Pre-arranged arrest/self-surrender of an indicted fraud defendant at the agency office, task force building, or courthouse: sworn fraud investigator (e.g., state insurance-fraud bureau, Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, IRS-CI) verifies identity, informs subject of the warrant, applies handcuffs, pat-searches, secures property, transports in a caged vehicle and completes booking/fingerprinting.

Warrant arrest at the subject's private residence, often at dawn and often paired with a search warrant: team knocks/announces, controls occupants, pets and unknown rooms, physically takes the named subject into custody, cuffs, searches for weapons, allows dressing/childcare arrangements, then walks the subject out and transports for booking.

Arrest at the subject's workplace or business premises (clinic, agency office, auto shop, dealership) during business hours, with employees and customers present: locate the subject amid staff, take custody discreetly, cuff and search, escort out past bystanders, transport for processing.

Arrest at a staged meeting or public location arising from an undercover/sting operation (parking lot, restaurant, curbside, hotel lobby): investigators converge on the subject, control hands, cuff and search on the spot, seize evidence such as phone or cash, then transport.

Arrest of an uncooperative, fleeing, intoxicated or medically compromised subject: short foot pursuit or hands-on control, take-down and restraint with proportionate force, handcuffing of a resisting person, medical screening, and secure transport.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robot ("DubBot"), Dublin, Ohio Police Department
sources.title: Ohio Police Fire Robocop for Helping Make Zero Arrests and Failing to Issue a Single Ticket
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous police/security robot in US service, the Knightscope K5, patrols but has no arms or manipulators and made zero arrests, tickets, or police reports during a 10-month municipal police deployment in a parking garage.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed law-enforcement robot to the task (patrolling and responding to persons on institutional premises); it establishes that fielded autonomous police robots neither physically take custody of people nor generate arrests.

sources.system: Lubbock Regional Bomb Squad tactical robot

sources.title: Wanted man barricaded in Lubbock motel room shot, gassed out and taken into custody
sources.claim: In the best-known case of a police robot physically subduing a wanted subject, the machine was a human-driven bomb-squad robot; a human operator drove it onto the suspect and a SWAT team then took the person into custody.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically restraining a wanted person for arrest. It does not transfer positively — control was continuous teleoperation and the custody, cuffing and transport steps were performed by human officers.

instances.label: Scheduled in-home installation visit for a chronic-care patient's remote patient monitoring kit: assess the dwelling's power, Wi-Fi/cellular coverage and available surfaces; unbox a hub/tablet, blood-pressure cuff, weight scale and pulse oximeter; route and plug power and cables; join the home network or a cellular gateway; Bluetooth-pair each peripheral; position equipment within the patient's reach; run a test vital-sign transmission to the monitoring platform; orient the patient/caregiver and leave documentation. Cluttered rooms, pets, variable furniture and unknown network conditions.

In-home repair/troubleshooting visit after a home telehealth device stops transmitting: locate the equipment in the residence, diagnose in situ (unplugged or damaged cables, dead batteries, replaced ISP router, moved cellular gateway, deleted app, failed Bluetooth pairing, sensor misplacement), re-seat or replace hardware, re-provision the tablet, re-pair peripherals, verify data reaches the clinical dashboard, re-train the patient.

Remote troubleshooting of a home telehealth application/system by phone or video with the patient or family member performing the hands-on steps in the home under the specialist's direction: guide power-cycling, re-pairing, app reinstall/reauthentication; push server-side or MDM configuration changes; if unresolved, ship a preconfigured replacement device and walk the patient through the swap.

Install or service telehealth endpoints and monitoring devices in institutional residences that function as the patient's home (assisted-living apartment, group home, skilled-nursing room): mount or place the video endpoint/tablet, connect to the facility network and power, pair peripherals, test a clinical video visit with staff and resident present, note issues with facility IT policy and Wi-Fi coverage.

Pre-deployment staging and kitting at the health system's telehealth depot/clinic workroom before equipment goes to the patient's home: pull the tablet, hub, cuff, scale and cables for the ordered program; enroll/image the tablet, power it on and tap through enrollment; pair peripherals and run a functional/connectivity check; assemble instructions and pack the kit for courier or mail shipment.

instances.label: Data center / colocation / large server room, fiber layer: replace a failed optical transceiver or fiber jumper, clean connector end-faces, execute cross-connect moves/adds/changes at patch panels or an optical distribution frame, and verify optical power and link before closing the ticket.

Enterprise MDF/IDF wiring closet: swap a failed access switch, small router, firewall, PoE injector or power-supply module — unrack the dead unit, rack the replacement, reconnect 12-48 copper patch cords to the correct ports, restore config, and verify all links come up.

Occupied user space (office, school, hospital ward, warehouse floor): replace a ceiling-mounted wireless access point, re-terminate or replace a wall jack and its drop cable, pull a new Cat6 run above drop ceilings, swap desk patch cords — ladder or lift work around furniture and people.

Scheduled maintenance window, comms-room connection hygiene: reseat line cards, optics and cables that show errors, clean suspect fiber ends, replace marginal jumpers, and re-verify light levels and error counters.

Scheduled maintenance window, comms-room electro-mechanical PM: clean dust filters and chassis fans, swap fan and power-supply modules, replace UPS batteries, dress and label cabling, connect a console cable for a firmware upgrade and power-cycle the device.

Remote / outdoor / industrial site: replace a hardened switch, outdoor AP, antenna or media converter in a weatherproof cabinet, plant-floor enclosure, retail back room, or unstaffed branch; reseal the enclosure, field-terminate or splice cabling, and test the link.

sources.title: Soon at DE-CIX: Two new patch robots
sources.claim: DE-CIX's patch robot, mounted on an optical distribution frame at the Frankfurt internet exchange, has been in production since 2018 and provisions or upgrades customer fiber ports in minutes without a technician physically intervening.

sources.system: Telescent G4 Network Topology Manager (robotic patch panel)
sources.title: Automated Telemetry for 5G and Data Center Fiber Monitoring — Telescent
sources.claim: Telescent's Network Topology Manager is a commercial single-rack robotic fiber cross-connect that reconfigures, monitors and cleans fiber connections under software control, deployed by data center and network operators.

sources.system: Tripp Lite Robotic Fiber Panel System (RFPS)
sources.title: Eaton Robotic Fiber Patch Panel System, LC Duplex, Multimode
sources.claim: Eaton/Tripp Lite sells a robotic fiber patch panel whose two robotic arms make and break physical fiber connections between switches and servers without on-site manual intervention, reconfiguring a connection in about 50 seconds.

sources.system: Microsoft Research modular datacenter robots (transceiver manipulation robot)
sources.title: Future AI Infrastructure - Microsoft Research: Robotics
sources.claim: Microsoft Research's datacenter robotics program has built dexterous robots that autonomously manipulate optical transceivers and ... in cluttered racks, including fiber cleaning and installation; the work is characterized as early-stage modular robotics rather than production deployment.

sources.title: Self-maintaining [networked] systems: The rise of datacenter robotics! (ACM HotNets '24)
sources.claim: In a peer-reviewed HotNets 2024 paper, Microsoft describes robots that perform common network maintenance tasks — reseating and cleaning optical transceivers ... — under software control.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: routine maintenance/standard repair of networking hardware (transceivers, fiber jumpers) in racks; objects and precision are those of the rated task.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Enables Five Super Data Centers to Support Double 11
sources.claim: Alibaba Cloud reports a second-generation Tianxun O&M robot operating in its data halls that inspects, locates and replaces faulty hard disks without human intervention, in about four minutes per disk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous replacement of a failed rack-mounted field-replaceable unit inside a data hall. It transfers only partially — disks sit in tool-free, cable-free carriers, whereas network devices require unplugging and re-plugging patch cords and rack fasteners — so it supports in-hall module swapping but not cabled network-device replacement.

sources.title: Video shows robotic installation Cat 6 cabling above drop ceiling
sources.claim: The only demonstrated robot for pulling communications cable above drop ceilings is a remote-controlled inspection platform, not an autonomous installer.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (in-building structured cabling), but the platform is remote-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: SoftBank Corp. Develops "Robot-friendly" Server Rack to Enable Automation at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank has designed a cableless, 'robot-friendly' server rack intended to let robots install and replace units, but robot integration is stated as a future test, not a demonstrated capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (rack-unit replacement), but the source describes a rack design plus planned robot testing — a roadmap, not a demonstrated robotic completion, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Install new hardware or software systems or components, ensuring integration with existing network systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Data center, colocation cage, or enterprise server room: rack-mount a new switch, router, firewall, or server; land power, run copper/fiber patch cords or order the cross-connect, label, bring the link up and verify integration with the existing fabric (VLANs, routing, monitoring). Institution-controlled facility, standard 19-inch racks and patch fields, gear delivered on a cart or lift.

Building or campus rollout: mount and cable wireless access points on ceilings and walls, pull and terminate horizontal cabling, install and patch switches in IDF/telecom closets, hang IP cameras - inside occupied offices, classrooms or clinics, with ladders, plenum spaces and conduit that vary room to room.

End-user or lab device work: install a NIC/PCIe card or SFP module in a desktop or lab server, set up a docking station, IP phone or printer at a user's desk, cable it to the wall jack, and confirm it registers on the network.

Software-only install/upgrade: push a new switch/router OS image or firmware, install network management or monitoring software, agents, licenses or drivers on existing servers and devices, and verify interoperability with the existing network - performed from a console or remotely, with no physical handling of equipment.

Field/branch/remote site: install a router, firewall, switch, wireless bridge or industrial network gear at a branch office, retail store, warehouse, plant floor, or outdoor pole/cabinet; site layout, power, mounting surfaces and weather differ site to site.

sources.system: DE-CIX patch robots (Patchy McPatchbot, Sir Patchalot, Margaret Patcher)
sources.title: DE-CIX Frankfurt 2020: Capacity increased, provisioning automated
sources.claim: DE-CIX operates fully automated 'patch robots' live at its Frankfurt internet-exchange data center sites; the gantry robots plug fiber into an optical distribution frame so customer ports are connected or upgraded without a technician physically intervening.
sources.transferJustification: Physically installing and integrating a new network connection - the patch/cross-connect step of bringing new network hardware onto an existing production network - performed in a purpose-built robotic patch frame with the same connectors and precision as human patching.

sources.title: DE-CIX migrates Frankfurt data center without disruption using patch robot
sources.claim: A DE-CIX patch robot independently executed the physical re-patching of roughly 450 customer connections during a live Frankfurt data center migration, with no reported errors.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical-layer install/integration work as connecting newly installed network hardware into a live network, at production quality, inside a purpose-built robotic frame.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM / G5 Robotic Patch Panel
sources.title: Telescent Introduces Highest Density Optical Circuit Switches for 1.6T DR4 and DR8 Interconnects in GPU Clusters
sources.claim: Telescent sells and has deployed robotic fiber patch-panel / optical cross-connect systems (G4 NTM, G5) that make and break physical fiber connections in data centers and carrier networks under remote software control, including a 2022 deployment by MOX Networks and 2026 high-density GPU-cluster systems.
sources.transferJustification: Installing and integrating new fiber links between existing and newly added equipment is the physical-integration half of this task; the robot performs it autonomously inside its own purpose-built enclosure and verifies the link with built-in diagnostics.

sources.title: SoftBank Corp. Develops "Robot-friendly" Server Rack to Enable Automation at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank developed a cable-less 'robot-friendly' server rack with blind-mate power, network and cooling connectors so that a robot installs or replaces a server simply by pushing it into a slot, eliminating manual cabling.

sources.system: Lifter robot + CTU container robot with robot-friendly rack
sources.title: Inside Look: How SoftBank Corp. is Creating "Robot-friendly" Environments at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank describes the robotic install workflow in test at its Hokkaido Tomakomai AI data center: a container robot delivers the server and a lifter robot uses camera QR recognition and laser positioning to place it in the specified rack slot, with LiDAR obstacle detection for safety.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot at Novva; Alibaba Tianxun; Switch Sentry
sources.title: Who's a good bot? Deploying robot dogs at data centers
sources.claim: Industry analysis of data center robotics: robots in ordinary human-run data halls are mostly monitoring, security or inspection pilots; the robot-maintained data center remains unachieved, with Alibaba's Tianxun disk-swap robot cited as one of the few hardware-handling deployments (hot-swap disk bays only, no racking or cabling of new equipment).
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the negative bound: no fielded robot racks, cables and integrates new network hardware in a standard human-run (E2) data hall or office building.

sources.system: Cisco IOS XR / IOS XE Zero Touch Provisioning
sources.title: Provision Network Devices using Zero Touch Provisioning (Cisco NCS 560 Series, IOS XR 25.x)
sources.claim: Zero-Touch Provisioning is a shipping vendor capability that automatically installs or upgrades a device's software image, application packages and configuration files when equipment is brought onto the network, without a technician performing the software install.
sources.transferJustification: The software-install instance involves no action on the physical world, so no robotic system is required; this named commercial system performs the whole install/upgrade and integration step, from image download to running configuration.

tasks.label: Test computer software or hardware, using standard diagnostic testing equipment and procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Remote/console diagnostics from a NOC desk or laptop: ping, traceroute, throughput tests, packet captures, interface and error-counter checks, log and configuration verification, testing a software patch or firmware image in a lab VM. Purely informational output; no equipment is handled.

Copper cabling and link certification in a campus or office building: carrying a cable certifier, wiremap tester and tone generator to wall jacks, telecom closets and patch panels to certify new drops or find a faulty run, working around occupied cubicles and in cramped closets.

Optical/physical-layer testing in a data center or MDF: optical power meter, OTDR, connector inspection scope and loopback checks on fiber links and transceivers between racks, verifying light levels and link validation before turning a circuit up.

Bench testing suspect hardware in the IT shop: a switch, router, access point, NIC or SFP brought to the bench, powered up, run through vendor POST/diagnostic utilities, loopback and port tests, components swapped to isolate the fault, result recorded in the ticket.

Desk-side or branch-site testing: at a user's desk, test the PC's NIC and drivers, patch cord, wall port, VoIP phone or wireless signal with a handheld tester and diagnostic utilities, swap a cable or module to confirm the fault, while the user and their belongings occupy the space.

sources.system: Telescent G5 Robotic Patch Panel / Network Topology Manager
sources.title: Smart Patch Panels: Revolutionizing Fiber Optic Network Management — Telescent
sources.claim: Telescent's G5 robotic patch panel is a commercial robotic system installed in data centers and carrier facilities that physically makes and breaks fiber connections under software control and carries optical power monitoring plus an optional OTDR for on-demand physical-layer diagnostics.
sources.transferJustification: Running OTDR and optical-power tests on links is precisely 'testing hardware using standard diagnostic testing equipment and procedures' for optical plant; the robot both connects the link and runs the instrument, replacing the technician's patch-and-test visit.

sources.title: Telescent Showcases Robotic 16,128-Fiber Optical Switch - Converge Digest
sources.claim: The same robotic system runs built-in link-validation diagnostics before a circuit is activated, i.e. it performs the test-and-certify step on fibers presented to its panel.

sources.system: Keysight automation optical switches including the G5 Robotic Patch Panel
sources.title: Automation Optical Switches | Keysight
sources.claim: Keysight sells the G5 robotic patch panel within its commercial lab test-automation portfolio, where robotic fiber patching connects equipment under test to test instruments inside a test lab.
sources.transferJustification: Lab test automation is the fixtured (E1) form of link and equipment testing: the robot presents the link to instruments and the test sequence executes without a technician patching cables.

sources.title: How RAM is Made: Automated Binning, Manufacturing, & Burn-in Testing | Factory Tours | GamersNexus
sources.claim: In V-Color's Taiwan facility, robotic arms load computer memory modules into test fixtures and run standardized pass/fail and burn-in diagnostics continuously, one arm testing roughly 23,000 modules per day with only two operators overseeing the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Bench testing suspect computer hardware — seat the component, run the standard diagnostic, record pass/fail, retest under different settings — is the same loop: robotic mating of computer hardware with a test fixture plus automated execution of a diagnostic procedure.

sources.title: Samsung - A Remote Test Lab for Samsung's Home Appliances | OptoFidelity
sources.claim: OptoFidelity supplies commercial robotic test systems that manipulate a fixtured device under test with camera-based DUT positioning and run standardized hardware/software test procedures with automated reporting, including Microsoft Windows HCK touch certification testing.
sources.transferJustification: Driving a device's interface and measuring its responses against a standard test procedure is the bench-test variant of this task, executed by a robot on a fixtured unit in a purpose-built work cell.

sources.system: Data center robotics fleet (inspection robots, remote-hands robots)
sources.title: How Robotics Is Re-Engineering Data Center Construction and Operations | Data Center Frontier
sources.claim: An industry review of data center robotics as of early 2026 finds that live facilities use robots mainly for autonomous inspection patrols, while physical 'remote hands' work is teleoperated and cabling and patching remain unsolved dexterity and perception problems.

sources.system: Microsoft Research modular datacenter robots (transceiver manipulation robot)
sources.title: Microsoft Research details early-stage modular robotics for data centers - DCD
sources.claim: Microsoft Research has an early-stage prototype robot that uses vision to navigate cluttered rack cabling and reseat, plug or unplug optical transceivers in data center racks; the team describes the effort as at the very start of the journey.

sources.system: Tianxun data center O&M robot (second generation)
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba reports a second-generation Tianxun robot operating in five of its data centers that inspects, locates and replaces faulty hard disks without human intervention in about four minutes per disk.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest deployed analogue to in-rack hardware verification in a human-run facility; cited to bound what mobile data center robots do today (telemetry-driven disk swap in robot-adapted hyperscale aisles) rather than instrument-based link testing.

tasks.label: Install or repair network cables, including fiber optic cables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Data center or carrier POP: install, replace or re-route fiber jumpers/cross-connects between patch panels and equipment ports; clean connectors, dress the jumper through managers, verify light/link.
Enterprise telecom room / IDF rack: install, replace and dress copper Cat6 patch cords between patch panel ports and switch ports; correct mis-patches, verify link and label.

Pull new horizontal cable runs in an occupied office/commercial building: ladders, lifting ceiling tiles, J-hooks and sleeves above the ceiling, fishing walls and risers from the IDF to work-area outlets, avoiding HVAC/electrical and existing cable.
Terminate and certify copper: strip jacket, arrange and trim pairs, punch down to patch panel and keystone jacks or crimp 8P8C plugs, then test/certify the link with a field tester.
Fiber work at a splice tray/enclosure or closet: field-terminate or fusion-splice fibers, clean and inspect endfaces, route into trays, test with power meter/OTDR.

Repair a faulty or damaged run in service: tone/locate the fault, then repair or replace cable under desks, in floor boxes, in a riser, or in conduit between buildings, often while users are working nearby.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM robotic patch panel / Optical Circuit Switch
sources.title: Telescent Secures Major Order from Top Cloud and AI Hyperscaler
sources.claim: Telescent's robotic fiber patch panel / optical cross-connect physically automates tens of thousands of fiber links, replacing manual cross-connect work; ordered at scale by a top cloud/AI hyperscale data center operator.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM robotic patch panel
sources.title: Telescent Bags Order from Hyperscale Data Center Operator
sources.claim: The Telescent product is a robotic patch-panel that makes latched all-optical connections and is reconfigured and diagnosed under software control, i.e. the physical connect/disconnect is executed by the machine.

sources.title: The Telescent NTM enables physical layer automation (DOE SBIR success story)
sources.claim: Telescent's robot autonomously computes and executes strand reconfigurations inside a dense fixtured fiber array without entangling strands (Knots-Braids-Strands algorithm), per a US DOE SBIR success story.

sources.title: MOX Networks to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform
sources.claim: A named network operator (MOX Networks) deployed the G4 NTM as a remotely reconfigurable fiber patch-panel and cross-connect with diagnostics on a live long-haul route.

sources.title: Automatic Cut, Strip and Crimp Machine | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Fully automatic wire-processing machines cut, strip and terminate conductors without an operator in a fenced factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory cable termination. The copper-termination half of the network tech's job (jacket strip, conductor handling, terminate to a connector, quality-monitored) is performed on comparable multiconductor cable at comparable or finer precision when the cable is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Fully automatic crimping machines - Schleuniger
sources.claim: Schleuniger's fully automatic CrimpCenter machines perform cutting, stripping, crimping and related terminating steps; companion automatic machines process multiconductor and shielded cables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory cable termination on multiconductor/shielded cable, the same physical operations (jacket and conductor stripping, terminating) the technician performs by hand on Cat6, done unattended when the cable is fixtured.

sources.system: WL-SJ101 automatic Ethernet cable/patch cord production line
sources.title: Network Cable Machine Fully Automatic Ethernet Cable Production Line for RJ45/RJ11/Cat6 and Patch Cord Cable Crimp Machine (WL-SJ101)
sources.claim: A commercially sold production line terminates Ethernet cable end-to-end automatically: cut, strip, twist, crimp, vision check, insert the network connector and test the finished cord.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point for the termination/test instance and for the plug-into-port step: the machine terminates RJ45 ends and inserts/tests the connector, the same operations the technician performs, with the cable presented by the line.

sources.system: Rocsys M1 / ROC-1 autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic arms autonomously locate a port, insert a power connector, and disconnect it, with a claimed 99.9%+ plug-in success rate in ... operating environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cable-connector mating into a socket. It substantiates that a machine can locate a port, insert a cable connector and confirm the connection repeatedly at production reliability; in a fixtured E1 patching cell the port position is known, making the task easier than on a parked vehicle.

sources.title: Rocsys to supply autonomous charging solutions for electric yard tractors at Port of Oakland
sources.claim: Rocsys ROC-1 autonomous charging systems were contracted for electric yard tractors at a container terminal, showing deployed robotic connector insertion in daily operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated autonomous mating of a cable connector into a receptacle in daily industrial operation, the physical action at the core of patching a cord into a port.

sources.system: Model-based connector mating with ArtiMinds Robot Task Model
sources.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation
sources.claim: Force-controlled robotic connector mating (the connector family benchmarked on the NIST task board includes RJ45) is implemented with commercial robot-programming tooling for wire harness installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting small multi-pin electrical connectors (RJ45-class) into mating ports under force control — the same precision and compliance problem as seating a patch cord plug in a fixtured panel port.

sources.title: Automated fiber switch with path verification enabled by an AI-powered multi-task mobile robot
sources.claim: A mobile robot with a collaborative arm that physically switches fiber patch cables in racks, with optical path verification, exists only as a research demonstration.

sources.developer: Fiber Optic Center (industry account of splicer automation)
sources.title: Automation in Connector Assembly is Essential for Connectivity
sources.claim: Core-alignment fusion splicers align, splice and quality-test fibers hands-free once the prepared fiber is placed in the fixture.

sources.system: Modular fiber pigtail assembly system with Epson robots
sources.title: Case Studies: Assembly of Fiber Optics Patch Cords | EPSON Robots
sources.claim: A robotic cell assembles fiber optic pigtails: fiber is loaded into pallets and downstream stations automatically strip, clean and process the fiber ends.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fiber connectorization in a fixtured cell — the strip/clean/terminate/inspect sequence the technician performs by hand at a splice tray, executed by machine when the fiber is presented in a pallet fixture.

sources.title: Video shows robotic installation Cat 6 cabling above drop ceiling
sources.claim: The only demonstrated robot installing Cat 6 cable above a drop ceiling is a camera-equipped platform driven by a human operator over a live video feed.

sources.title: Development of Cable-Laying Robot Based on Reconfigurable Single-Actuator-Wave Units
sources.claim: Autonomous cable-laying robots for building ceiling spaces remain laboratory prototypes benchmarked against earlier prototypes, not fielded installation systems.

sources.system: Robot-friendly server rack with blind-mate optical connectors
sources.title: Inside Look: How SoftBank Corp. is Creating "Robot-friendly" Environments at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank built a purpose-built 'robot-friendly' server rack with blind-mate optical/power connectors so that a robot makes the network connection by pushing the server into the rack, eliminating manual cabling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making the physical network connection in a rack. It shows the connection step is machine-executable only when the rack is rebuilt around the machine (fixtured blind-mate presentation), i.e. an E1 setting, not among as-found cabling.

tasks.label: Install and configure wireless networking equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Enterprise office/campus build-out: per a wireless site survey, mount several ceiling APs in a drop-tile or hard-lid office ceiling (ladder work, bracket to grid/anchor to deck), dress and plug the PoE drop above the tile, then adopt the AP into the WLAN controller, apply SSID/RF profile, and validate coverage with a survey tool.

Adds/moves/changes in an occupied facility (office suite, clinic, school, retail store): replace a failed or end-of-life AP at an existing mount point, reuse the existing cable drop, re-seat bracket, re-cable, provision the replacement in the controller, and verify clients associate — done around people and furniture during business hours.

Small business, branch, or home-office install: place/wall-mount a wireless gateway, router, or mesh AP near a modem/switch in a closet, under a desk, or on a shelf; connect power and Ethernet, then configure SSID, WPA, channels, DHCP, and test throughput in a space taken as found.

Warehouse, manufacturing, or outdoor campus: mount high-bay APs and antennas at 25-40 ft from a scissor lift or on structural steel/racking, and install/aim outdoor point-to-point bridge antennas on rooftops or masts; weatherproof connections, ground, then configure and align the link.

Bench/IT-room staging and rack work: bulk pre-stage a batch of APs or rack a wireless LAN controller in the telecom room — unbox, connect power and patch cable to a switch, upgrade firmware, push base configuration, verify the device joins and passes checks, label and repack for field deployment.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially available semi-autonomous mobile robot that drills and marks overhead holes for MEP/installation work from BIM data on construction sites — it automates only the hole-drilling sub-step, not device mounting, cabling, or commissioning, and it works under operator supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead drilling/anchor layout for building services installs. It shows what is automated for in-building overhead work today — drilling and marking only — and therefore does not cover mounting a wireless AP, terminating/plugging its cable, or configuring and validating it.

sources.title: A Production System for a New Era — The Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots can transform a job site!
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy performs autonomous two-arm overhead installation work on real building sites (inserting ceiling hanger bolts, holding and screwing ceiling boards), the closest existing analog to fastening a device to a building ceiling; it handles standard panels/bolts and does no cable termination or device commissioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead ceiling installation on construction sites. Transfer is limited: the objects are uniform boards/bolts placed on a cleared, pre-planned grid, with no network connector insertion, no device power-up, and no configuration/verification step.

sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun robot autonomously locates and replaces failed hard disks in operating data centers, showing that hands-off swapping of IT hardware works only inside racks and aisles engineered around the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically installing/replacing network-attached IT hardware in racks. Comparable object class and precision, but the environment is a purpose-engineered rack/aisle, and the work is a slot-in carrier swap rather than overhead mounting plus cable termination.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM robotic fiber cross-connect
sources.title: MOX Networks to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform
sources.claim: Telescent's G4 Network Topology Manager is a deployed robotic patch-panel that makes and breaks physical fiber network connections on command inside its own enclosure, i.e. autonomous connector handling only within purpose-built hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically connecting network equipment. It substantiates autonomous make/break of network connectors, but only for fibers pre-loaded into a machine built around the robot; it cannot mount or cable a device in a building.

sources.system: Circuit Check 6000 Series Rotary Handler (functional test system)
sources.title: Rotary Automation - Circuit Check
sources.claim: Circuit Check's 6000 Series rotary handler is a commercial automated test cell in which a robotic handler presents each device into drop-in fixtures that mate its connectors, run functional test, and perform flash programming — the standard way devices are electrically connected and loaded with firmware/configuration unattended in a fenced, purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured connection and firmware/configuration loading of electronic devices. Same object class (network device with edge connectors), same operations (mate connector, power, load config, verify pass/fail), performed unattended when the work is presented in fixtures — the E1 form of bench staging.

sources.system: Behavioral-cloning connector insertion policy (robot arm with grayscale camera and force-torque sensor)
sources.title: Behavioral Cloning for Robotic Connector Assembly: An Empirical Study
sources.claim: Recent research demonstrates autonomous vision/force-based robotic insertion of multiple connector types at about 93% average success, i.e. reliable-but-not-industrial-grade plugging of connectors on a fixtured bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting electrical connectors (the plug-in step of installing wireless gear). Comparable objects and sub-millimetre precision, but demonstrated only with the socket fixtured on a lab bench, not on a device mounted overhead in a building.

instances.label: New-hire / new-machine workstation setup at a desk in a corporate office: unbox laptop, dock and two monitors, assemble monitor stands or arms, route and plug power, DisplayPort/HDMI/USB-C and ethernet cables behind and under the desk, connect keyboard/mouse/headset, power on and verify the corporate image boots and the user can log in, tidy cables.

Batch provisioning at an IT staging bench/depot: a pallet of new laptops or desktops is unboxed, each connected to power and ethernet (or a docking fixture), PXE/Autopilot/Jamf imaging and application installs are run and verified, asset tags applied, machines repacked or racked for delivery.

Desk-side refresh / move-add-change at an occupied desk or cubicle: crawl under the desk, disconnect a mix of legacy cables from the old PC, remove it, install and cable the replacement (or relocate the kit to a new desk), migrate user data and profile, verify peripherals and printers work, remove the old equipment.

Shared peripheral installation in an office: unbox and site a network printer/MFP, scanner, badge reader or VoIP phone; strip shipping tape and foam, insert toner/ink and load paper trays, connect power and network cabling, install and configure drivers on the users' machines, run a test print/scan.

Conference/huddle room or shared-space equipment setup: mount or place a display and camera, run cables through wall plates, grommets and furniture, connect the room PC/codec, pair peripherals, configure and test the room system for employee use.

Remote/home-office employee setup: equipment shipped to a private home, with the specialist either travelling to the home to install and cable it or verifying/directing the installation and completing OS/software configuration remotely.

sources.system: HIL-SERL (Franka arm with wrist cameras, human-in-the-loop RL)

sources.title: Precise and Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: HIL-SERL trained policies autonomously perform computer-hardware assembly and cable tasks on a fixtured lab bench — RAM insertion, SSD assembly, USB connector grasp-insertion, USB cable clipping and IKEA panel assembly — at 100% success after 1–2.5 hours of training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: motherboard/computer assembly. The connectors (USB, SSD/RAM edge connectors) and cable-routing/clipping are the same class of objects and insertion tolerances as plugging monitor, dock, power and network cables during workstation setup; human corrections occur only during training, and the learned policy executes autonomously.

sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory autonomously assembles and disassembles laptop PCs and servers in a purpose-built cell, including removing and refitting internal components; ABB Robotics is partnering and investing to deploy these microfactories for data-center equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic (dis)assembly of laptops and servers. It handles exactly the IT hardware a support specialist sets up or swaps — unfastening, removing and refitting components and internal connectors — but only inside a fixtured microfactory cell, not at a user's desk.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume device commissioning/reconditioning. Physically connecting each device and running erase/image/diagnostic workflows is the same work as bench-imaging a batch of corporate machines; objects are comparable consumer-electronics devices, and the cell is purpose-built.

sources.title: Refurbished Device Diagnostics | MATT Robot Testing Automation
sources.claim: The MATT robot is a commercial test-automation robot that physically interacts with laptops, tablets, phones and control panels for device commissioning, refurbishment and end-of-line ...; in refurbishment cells one operator supervises multiple robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated device commissioning and verification. Driving a device's screen/buttons through setup and test scripts is the physical half of verifying an imaged machine works, on the same laptop/tablet hardware, inside a fixtured testing cell.

sources.system: Eureka Controller / Eureka 3D Camera force-controlled connector insertion
sources.title: Automated Connector Insertion in Automotive Wire Harness Assembly
sources.claim: Eureka Robotics supplies a commercial 3D-vision plus force-control solution in which a robot grips a connector on a slider and inserts it into the mating connector without pin damage, automating a previously manual wire-harness connector-insertion step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial connector mating. Multi-pin connector insertion with vision plus force control is the core physical skill of cabling a workstation (power, DP/HDMI, USB, RJ45); it is demonstrated only in fixtured production cells.

sources.system: Telescent G4/G5 robotic patch panel (automated fiber cross-connect)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated physical cabling. It shows reliable production-grade robotic cable plugging/unplugging, but only into a purpose-built robotic patch-panel enclosure where every port position is known to the machine.

sources.title: SoftBank Corp. Develops “Robot-friendly” Server Rack to Enable Automation at Data Centers
sources.claim: To let robots install and replace servers, SoftBank had to design a new cable-less server rack, indicating that robotic IT-hardware installation currently requires re-engineering the environment around the machine rather than working with existing human-oriented cabling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of IT hardware in racks. Cited as context for the ceiling: the leading approach removes cables entirely and rebuilds the rack for the robot, rather than having a robot cable equipment in an as-found human setting.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plugging of a standardized connector outside a fenced cell. It shows connector mating tolerant of some pose variation, but the connector type, mounting and bay geometry are purpose-built for the robot, unlike an office desk.

instances.label: Corporate IT depot/stockroom: per a ticket or order sheet, the tech pulls a new laptop or desktop from stock, unboxes it, inspects it for shipping damage and correct configuration, checks the serial/asset tag against the order, gathers the matching charger, dock, mouse/keyboard, and repacks or stages the bundle on a cart for hand-off to the user.

Bulk refresh / mass deployment staging (school district, university, or corporate refresh): dozens to hundreds of identical laptops or Chromebooks in a staging room; each unit is unboxed, visually inspected, serial recorded against the purchase order/user roster, asset-tagged, re-boxed and carted by destination building.

Peripheral and accessory orders: tech reads the order sheet and picks monitors, docks, headsets, keyboards, cables, toner from stockroom shelves, checks each box/item for damage and completeness, bundles and labels the order, and stages it for internal courier or desk-side delivery.

Returned/redeployed equipment: laptops and tablets returned from departing staff or loaner pools are inspected for cosmetic damage, missing keys/feet/screws and missing accessories, cleaned, condition-graded, matched to a pending equipment request, and prepped for reissue.

Large or specialty equipment: workstation-on-wheels carts, multifunction printers, conference-room AV kits, ruggedized or clinical/lab devices; the tech assembles/inspects the unit, verifies all cables, mounts, media and consumables against the order sheet, and readies it for delivery to the department.

MSP/small-business field variant: technician meets the shipment at the client's own office or home office, opens cartons on whatever surface is available, inspects the gear against the order paperwork, and sets it aside/stages it for the user.
