instances.label: Walkthrough of an occupied, finished commercial building (office suite, school, hospital wing, retail) ahead of a structured-cabling / AP / camera / AV deployment: engineer walks floors with drawings, opens telecom rooms and enclosures, lifts ceiling tiles and looks above the grid to find existing conduit, J-hooks, tray and sleeve capacity, checks core penetrations and fire-stopping, notes existing jack/device locations, measures prospective cable-run lengths, photographs conditions, and produces marked-up plans/survey notes feeding the design. Concealed pathways in walls and above ceilings are the crux of the deliverable.

Survey inside an industrial, logistics or IT facility where infrastructure is exposed: warehouse/distribution center, plant floor, data hall, or carrier central-office equipment room. Engineer documents rack/cabinet and device locations, overhead cable tray and conduit runs, ladder-rack routes, available rack units, port and power positions, mounting points for APs/antennas/cameras, and clearances. Layout is fixed, aisles are clear, and most of what must be recorded is visible overhead or on open racks.

Wireless RF / DAS / in-building cellular site survey of a facility: engineer walks the space with a survey kit (spectrum analyzer, survey adapter, AP-on-a-stick), takes passive/active measurements floor by floor, temporarily mounts and repositions test radios on a pole, notes attenuation from walls, racking and inventory, and from the measurements determines where APs/antennas must be located and how they will be cabled back to the IDF.

Cell tower or rooftop antenna site audit: engineer (or climbing crew) documents the physical configuration of the vertical asset — antenna, RRU and mount locations, azimuths, RAD centers, existing coax/fiber runs on the structure, remaining mount and tower space for new equipment — for a colocation, 5G upgrade or lease audit. Outdoors on a fenced, carrier-controlled compound or a controlled rooftop, weather permitting.

Ground-level cell-site and outside-plant survey: engineer inspects the compound and equipment shelter/outdoor cabinet interiors (rack space, power plant, breakers, grounding bar, cable entry ports), the ice bridge and conduit/duct entries, hand holes and pull boxes, and traces the feeder/pole or duct-bank route to the site. Requires opening cabinet doors and enclosures and often confined or below-grade access.

Rough-in / new-construction site walk of an unfinished building or renovation: engineer walks an active jobsite with drawings before ceilings close, verifying installed conduit stub-ups, sleeves, backboxes, cable tray and pathway routing against the design, noting conflicts with other trades, and capturing as-built positions of telecom pathways and device rough-ins. Site is cluttered, changes daily, and other trades are working.

sources.title: Scaling Cell Tower Inspections with 3D Tower Scan | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan's 3D Tower Capture is an autonomous drone capture mode that plans its own spiral flight path around telecom towers and produces 3D digital twins used for site inspection, post-installation verification and antenna/asset inventory management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is cell-tower inspection/asset inventory; it transfers because the deliverable is exactly the physical configuration of the site's devices (antenna/RRU placement, RAD centers, mounts, cable runs) captured in situ, the same determination the engineer makes on a tower site walk.

sources.system: Optelos telecom inspection platform (drone data capture + digital twin)
sources.title: Telecom Inspection Data Management | Optelos
sources.claim: Drone-captured digital twins of cell sites are used commercially by tower owners and carriers to review antenna placement, azimuths, mounts and RAD-center usage and to verify current tower configuration, installation space and available shelter rack space/power without repeat site visits.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed on carrier sites: determining the site's physical configuration (device locations, space, cable/power routing) from remotely captured data; cited for output relevance only, since capture autonomy is not established in this source.

sources.system: Skydio autonomous drones + Optelos inspection platform
sources.title: Partners Archives | Optelos
sources.claim: Optelos' cell-site inspection workflow is integrated with Skydio autonomous drones, so the capture leg of these commercial tower assessments is flown autonomously rather than hand-piloted.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy of the capture platform used for the cell-tower site-assessment task described in the Optelos evidence item.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Leica BLK ARC
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics’ Spot® | Geo Week News
sources.claim: The Leica BLK ARC laser-scanning module is a certified payload for Boston Dynamics Spot, enabling autonomous robotic scanning missions that document as-found site conditions in plants, warehouses ... for asset management and BIM modelling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous reality capture / as-built documentation of facilities; it transfers because the accepted output is a dimensioned record of visible equipment, tray and conduit positions in a working facility, which is what the engineer's site inspection records.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Leica BLK ARC at Turner Construction
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Leica Geosystems, operated by Turner Construction
sources.title: Automation in Construction - BLK Autonomy | Leica Geosystems
sources.claim: Turner Construction runs Spot carrying a BLK ARC on daily autonomous scanning missions at active jobsites; the captured data is compared against the coordinated BIM model ... confirm installed work matches design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is construction as-built/QA scanning on an active jobsite; it transfers because verifying installed rough-in (conduit, tray, boxes) against drawings is the same determination of physical configuration the telecom engineer makes on a rough-in site walk.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's lidar-equipped autonomous ground robots scan construction sites daily and check that installed elements match the plans, in production pilots such as a medical office building.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated progress/installation verification of MEP elements including conduit on unfinished jobsites; transfer holds because the objects, precision and cluttered site conditions match the telecom rough-in pathway inspection.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot at Novva Data Centers
sources.title: Who’s a good bot? Deploying robot dogs at data centers - DCD
sources.claim: Novva Data Centers operates a fleet of Spot robots that, after being taught the building layout, run their own patrol routes through the data halls and campus, with mapped positions for equipment not yet installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous patrol/inspection rounds in data halls; transfer holds for documenting rack and device positions in the same aisles, though it does not cover opening enclosures.

sources.title: Verity, On and Maersk Pilot RFID Technology with Autonomous Drones in Warehouse Inventory Management | Automation.com
sources.claim: Verity's drones fly fully autonomously through occupied warehouse aisles at night, locating and recording stock at rack positions with high reliability, in commercial deployments with logistics operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous indoor inventory location auditing at height in a working facility; it transfers to recording device/asset positions in warehouse and industrial interiors, though it does not address concealed pathways.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot / Orbit automated visual inspection
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot with Orbit for autonomous inspection missions in industrial workplaces, where a single robot and its sensor payloads autonomously cover an area, capture imagery and read instruments without an operator driving it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is routine autonomous equipment-inspection rounds in industrial facilities; it substantiates that repeatable in-situ visual data capture of fixed equipment can be done without continuous human control.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office move/add/change at user workstations: with facilities staff during a floor or team move, install or relocate VoIP handsets, docking stations, desk switches, headsets and monitors — unplug patch cords from wall jacks and devices, route cords under desks and through cubicle grommets, re-plug at the new desk, power up and verify the link/dial tone in an occupied office.

Wall/ceiling-mounted user connectivity devices: mount or remove wireless access points, DAS antennas, IP phones/intercoms or wall plates — locate the mounting point above a suspended ceiling or on drywall, install anchors and bracket, pull and terminate the Cat6 drop through plenum/conduit, seat the connector, dress the cable and verify PoE link, working from a ladder or lift with facilities escort.

Telecom room (IDF/MDF) work: rack-mount or remove edge switches, media converters, injectors and UPS units; terminate and dress copper/fiber to patch panels; add, move or remove patch cords for user ports; label ports and remove decommissioned gear from the closet.

Data center / server room: install, relocate or decommission network hardware serving user connectivity (switches, transceivers, cross-connects), run and connect fiber/copper patch leads between racks, label and verify circuits, in a standardized hot/cold-aisle facility.

Off-campus/field work: install or remove user connectivity equipment at a small remote site, teleworker home office, leased suite or building under fit-out — mount the CPE/router/AP where conditions allow, run and terminate cable in whatever pathway exists, connect and test with the site's occupants and landlord staff present.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM robotic patch panel
sources.title: MOX Announces New Telescent Automation Technology on its Latest Hillsboro to Portland Fiber Route
sources.claim: Telescent's G4 Network Topology Manager, a robotic fiber patch panel, is deployed on a carrier fiber route where fiber connections between network devices are provisioned, tested and delivered remotely without dispatching a technician — i.e., the robot performs the install/remove/relocate of physical connections inside a purpose-built chassis.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task family — installing, removing and relocating physical connectivity between user/customer ports — but performed inside a purpose-built robotic cross-connect enclosure rather than by hand at a patch field.

sources.title: Telescent's Automated Fiber Patch-Panel Solution Will be Highlighted at the 2023 Open Compute Project (OCP) Regional Summit
sources.claim: Telescent's automated fiber cross-connect platform is a commercial product line deployed globally for years by network and data center operators.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as patch-cord moves/adds/changes for user connectivity, executed by a robot in a purpose-built patch-panel environment.

sources.system: Eureka Robotics force-controlled connector insertion cell (Eureka 3D camera + force-torque sensing)
sources.title: Automated Connector Insertion in Automotive Wire Harness Assembly
sources.claim: A commercial robot cell mates electrical connectors on a moving automotive wire-harness line using 3D vision plus force-torque feedback, automating a connector-insertion task previously done manually.
sources.transferJustification: Plugging a data/power connector into a device or jack is the core physical act of installing or relocating user connectivity equipment; comparable connector sizes, insertion forces and alignment tolerances, here done in a fixtured industrial cell.

sources.title: Behavioral Cloning for Robotic Connector Assembly: An Empirical Study
sources.claim: A UR5e with a Robotiq gripper, wrist force-torque sensing and a camera learns connector insertion and achieves over 90% insertion success across five connector geometries with varying connector poses.
sources.transferJustification: Connector mating with pose variation is the precision-critical step of installing/relocating phones, docks, APs and patch cords; demonstrated on a fixtured benchtop workcell (E1-type setting).

sources.developer: UC Berkeley / Intrinsic (Luo, Xu, Levine et al.)
sources.title: Multi-Stage Cable Routing through Hierarchical Imitation Learning
sources.claim: A learned vision-based policy on a dual-arm robot autonomously performs multi-stage cable routing, manipulating a deformable cable through a series of ... on a fixtured board and recovering from failures.
sources.transferJustification: Dressing and routing a patch cord or drop cable into clips/managers is the cable-handling portion of installing user connectivity equipment; shown autonomously in a fixtured workcell.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Solution (screwdriver + screw feeder) for collaborative robots
sources.title: Screwdriving Solution — Universal Robots Marketplace
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic screwdriving end-effectors and Cartesian screwdriving cells fasten components autonomously in fixtured assembly stations.
sources.transferJustification: Mounting an access point bracket, wall plate or rack ear is a screw-fastening operation; commercial robotic screwdriving covers this step when the workpiece is fixtured and presented.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center O&M robot
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center — DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba Cloud states its second-generation Tianxun robot works without human intervention to locate and replace faulty hard disks in racks, in operation at five of its data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Removing and installing a blind-mate hardware module in a rack is the equipment install/remove step of this task; it does not cover patch-cord or building cabling work, so it supports only the module-swap portion.

sources.developer: Inspector Bots (also SuperDroid Robots drop-ceiling robots)
sources.title: Video shows robotic installation Cat 6 cabling above drop ceiling
sources.claim: Robotic platforms used by structured-cabling technicians to pull Cat 6 cable above suspended ceilings are remote-controlled vehicles driven by the technician, not autonomous installers.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-building cabling robot found; it is driven by an operator and only drags cable, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment at E2.
